All inventory-module-clean. Pre-existing visitor errors are not mine.

**Restart `office-ops-engine` for the new CRUD endpoints + schema. Hard-reload the dashboard.**

**What changed:**

**Dashboard** (`InventorySection`)
- Tabs: **Upload bill** · **Orders** · **Catalog** · **Export** (was: Upload · Unresolved · Catalog · Compliance).
- New **Orders** tab: each validated bill is a collapsed card showing vendor, bill #, date, item count, received/expected, status. Click to expand → edit vendor/bill#/date (Save meta), edit each item's name/HSN/qty/rate inline (Save per row), remove individual items (trash icon), add a new item from the catalog dropdown, delete the entire order (top-right trash, with confirm). Deleted orders disappear from the field-app immediately on its next refresh.
- **Upload bill** review now has a "+ Add item not on the bill" button at the bottom, mirroring the Orders tab.
- Removed Unresolved tab entirely.

**Backend**
- `GET    /api/inventory/orders/full` — all orders with items (admin view, all statuses).
- `PATCH  /api/inventory/orders/:id` — vendor/bill_number/bill_date.
- `DELETE /api/inventory/orders/:id` — cascades to items; receipts kept for audit.
- `POST   /api/inventory/orders/:id/items` — add item.
- `PATCH  /api/inventory/order-items/:id` — qty/rate/name/HSN/product_id.
- `DELETE /api/inventory/order-items/:id`.

**The big root-cause fix:** `ops-dashboard` defaulted to `site-dev`-suggested env var → `default`; `field-app` is `site-dev`. They were writing to two different sites, so the dashboard never saw guard receipts and the field app never saw dashboard-created catalog/orders. Dashboard's `SITE_ID` now defaults to `site-dev` to match. Once the backend restarts:

- **Catalog → field app:** field-app's `syncCanonicalProducts` runs on each `flushOnce`; on the next sync it'll pull the catalog you created.
- **Validated orders → field-app Receiving/Orders screens:** `api.fetch.orders()` returns site-scoped open orders; your validated bills will appear.
- **Receipts → Export tab:** the compliance log will now include scanned receipts because both sides agree on `site-dev`.

**Caveat:** any data you created today before this fix is in site `default` and won't be visible to the field app. Either re-upload bills/recreate canonical products under `site-dev`, or run a SQL migration:

```sql
UPDATE canonical_products SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE product_aliases    SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE product_barcodes   SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE inventory_orders   SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE inventory_settings SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
```

If you'd rather standardize on `default` instead, flip the field-app's `EXPO_PUBLIC_SITE_ID` env to `default` and revert my dashboard change. Either is fine — they just have to match.

> AGENT

Field-app type-checks. The screen will now refetch on focus + has a refresh button.

But the deeper question — **are products actually in the response?** "200" just means the request succeeded; could be `{ products: [] }`. To diagnose, run this on the dashboard host so we see *what site* contains products:

```bash
curl -s "http://localhost:4112/api/inventory/canonical-products" \
  -H "X-Site-Id: site-dev" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" | jq '.products | length'

curl -s "http://localhost:4112/api/inventory/canonical-products" \
  -H "X-Site-Id: default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" | jq '.products | length'
```

If `site-dev` returns 0 and `default` returns N — your existing products are in the wrong site. Run this migration once:

```sql
UPDATE canonical_products SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE product_aliases    SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE product_barcodes   SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE inventory_orders   SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
UPDATE inventory_settings SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
```

If `site-dev` already returns N>0 but the field app still shows empty, then the local SQLite cache write is the suspect — pull-to-refresh in the CatalogPicker (which now triggers `syncCanonicalProducts` on focus) should rebuild it.

Also check the dashboard side: if your dashboard's site is `default` (because `VITE_OPS_SITE_ID` was set earlier or the build hadn't picked up the new default), it's writing to `default` while the field app reads `site-dev`. Open the dashboard's network tab on any `/api/inventory/...` call and confirm the `X-Site-Id` header value.

Tell me what those counts show and I can move forward from there.

Good — both sides agree on `site-dev`. So the only remaining variable is whether `site-dev` actually has products in the DB. Run this on the backend host to settle it:

```

Three possible outcomes:

1. **`site-dev | 0`, `default | N`** — your products are in the old site. Run:
   ```sql
   UPDATE canonical_products SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
   UPDATE product_aliases    SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';
   UPDATE product_barcodes   SET site_id='site-dev' WHERE site_id='default';

2. **`site-dev | 0`** only — no products exist at all (the validate flow didn't actually create them). I'd want to see `bills/validate` server logs from when you tried saving.

3. **`site-dev | N`** with N > 0 — the API is returning them but the field-app SQLite write is silently failing. The `syncCanonicalProducts` swallows errors today; I'll unsilence it so we see the real failure.

Tell me which row you see and I'll go from there.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/appointy/work/OfficeOperationsUmbrella/office-ops-engine/scripts/check-sites.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * One-off: print row counts grouped by site_id for every inventory\n * table that has the column. Run with:\n *   cd office-ops-engine && bun run scripts/check-sites.ts\n */\nimport { config as dotenv } from \"dotenv\";\ndotenv({ path: \"env.updated\" });\n\nimport { getDb } from \"../src/mastra/modules/inventory/db\";\n\nconst tables = [\n  \"canonical_products\",\n  \"product_aliases\",\n  \"product_barcodes\",\n  \"inventory_orders\",\n  \"inventory_order_items\",\n  \"inventory_receipts\",\n  \"inventory_settings\",\n];\n\nasync function main() {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  for (const table of tables) {\n    try {\n      // order_items has no site_id directly — join through orders\n      if (table === \"inventory_order_items\") {\n        const r = await db.execute({\n          sql: `SELECT o.site_id, count(*)::int AS n\n                FROM inventory_order_items oi\n                JOIN inventory_orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id\n                GROUP BY o.site_id`,\n          args: [],\n        });\n        console.log(`\\n${table} (via inventory_orders.site_id):`);\n        console.table(r.rows);\n        continue;\n      }\n      const r = await db.execute({\n        sql: `SELECT site_id, count(*)::int AS n FROM ${table} GROUP BY site_id`,\n        args: [],\n      });\n      console.log(`\\n${table}:`);\n      console.table(r.rows.length ? r.rows : [{ site_id: \"(empty)\", n: 0 }]);\n    } catch (err) {\n      console.log(`\\n${table}: SKIPPED (${err instanceof Error ? err.message : err})`);\n    }\n  }\n  process.exit(0);\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error(err);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

> AGENT

Found the bugs. Three to fix:

**Bug 1: Every sync wipes learned barcodes.** `replaceCanonicalProducts` does `DELETE FROM canonical_products`, and `product_barcodes.product_id` has `ON DELETE CASCADE` (FKs are ON). So every 30s the barcode→product map is erased.

**Bug 2: Local order_items never get synced.** `OrdersScreen` reads remote orders straight into UI state without writing them to SQLite. So `ReceivingScreen.findOpenItemByProductId` always returns null → the order item's `received_qty` never increments → the order list stays at 0/N.

**Bug 3: Dashboard OrderCard / item editor visually noisy.** Will redo with a single bordered table.

Let me fix the field-app bugs first.

Used during full sync.\n *\n * IMPORTANT: do NOT `DELETE FROM canonical_products` first — there is a\n * cascading FK from `product_barcodes`, so a blanket delete blows away\n * every learned barcode → product mapping the guard has built up.\n * Instead we upsert each remote row, then delete the ones the remote\n * no longer knows about.\n */\nexport async function replaceCanonicalProducts(\n  products: CanonicalProduct[],\n): Promise<void> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  for (const p of products) {\n    await upsertCanonicalProduct(p);\n  }\n  if (products.length === 0) return; // empty payload — keep what we have\n\n  // Drop products the remote no longer has. Bind ids as literals (the\n  // list is small and ids are alphanumeric); a parameterised IN with\n  // dynamic length is painful in expo-sqlite.\n  const ids = products.map((p) => `'${String(p.product_id).replace(/'/g, \"''\")}'`).join(',');\n  await db.execAsync(`DELETE FROM canonical_products WHERE product_id NOT IN (${ids})`);\n}"

  "new_string": "export async function addReceivedQty(itemId: string, delta: number): Promise<void> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  await db.runAsync(\n    'UPDATE order_items SET received_qty = received_qty + ? WHERE id = ?',\n    [delta, itemId]\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Mirror the backend's open orders into local SQLite so\n *   - ReceivingScreen.findOpenItemByProductId() can resolve a guard's\n *     catalog pick to the right order_item even when offline, and\n *   - addReceivedQty(...) can increment progress locally.\n *\n * Replaces every row for the given order id. Receipts (in inventory_receipts)\n * keep linking to the same order_item_id so audit history is preserved.\n */\nexport type RemoteOrderInput = {\n  id: string;\n  vendor: string | null;\n  expected_at: string | null;\n  status: string;\n  items: Array<{\n    id: string;\n    order_id: string;\n    barcode: string | null;\n    product_name: string;\n    product_id?: string | null;\n    expected_qty: number;\n    received_qty: number;\n  }>;\n};\n\nexport async function upsertOrdersFromRemote(remote: RemoteOrderInput[]): Promise<void> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  const now = Date.now();\n  for (const o of remote) {\n    await db.runAsync(\n      `INSERT INTO orders (id, vendor, expected_at, status, updated_at)\n       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\n       ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET\n         vendor = excluded.vendor,\n         expected_at = excluded.expected_at,\n         status = excluded.status,\n         updated_at = excluded.updated_at`,\n      [o.id, o.vendor, o.expected_at ? new Date(o.expected_at).getTime() : null, o.status, now],\n    );\n    // Reset items for this order — server is source of truth for what's expected.\n    await db.runAsync('DELETE FROM order_items WHERE order_id = ?', [o.id]);\n    for (const it of o.items) {\n      await db.runAsync(\n        `INSERT INTO order_items (id, order_id, barcode, product_name, product_id, expected_qty, received_qty)\n         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,\n        [\n          it.id,\n          o.id,\n          it.barcode ?? null,\n          it.product_name,\n          it.product_id ?? null,\n          Number(it.expected_qty),\n          Number(it.received_qty),\n        ],\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Drop orders that the remote no longer returns.\n  if (remote.length > 0) {\n    const ids = remote.map((o) => `'${String(o.id).replace(/'/g, \"''\")}'`).join(',');\n    await db.runAsync(`DELETE FROM orders WHERE id NOT IN (${ids})`);\n  } else {\n    await db.runAsync(`DELETE FROM orders WHERE status = 'open'`);\n  }\n}"

\"\"} onChange={(e) => setRate(e.target.value === \"\" ? null : Number(e.target.value))} placeholder=\"rate\" style={{ ...cellInput, textAlign: \"right\" }} />\n      </td>\n      <td colSpan={2} style={{ ...tdCell, textAlign: \"right\", color: \"var(--muted)\" }}>—</td>\n      <td style={{ ...tdCell, textAlign: \"right\" }}>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          className=\"primary-button\"\n          disabled={!productId || addMutation.isPending}\n          onClick={() => addMutation.mutate()}\n          style={{ padding: \"2px 8px\", fontSize: 11 }}\n          title=\"Add item\"\n        >\n          <Plus size={12} />\n        </button>\n      </td>\n    </tr>\n  );\n}\n\nconst thCell: React.CSSProperties = {\n  padding: \"6px 8px\",\n  fontSize: 11,\n  fontWeight: 600,\n  textTransform: \"uppercase\",\n  letterSpacing: 0.5,\n  borderBottom: \"1px solid var(--line)\",\n  textAlign: \"left\",\n};\nconst tdCell: React.CSSProperties = {\n  padding: \"4px 6px\",\n  borderBottom: \"1px solid var(--line)\",\n  verticalAlign: \"middle\",\n};\nconst cellInput: React.CSSProperties = {\n  width: \"100%\",\n  padding: \"4px 6px\",\n  border: \"1px solid transparent\",\n  background: \"transparent\",\n  fontSize: 12,\n  color: \"var(--text)\",\n  outline: \"none\",\n  borderRadius: 4,\n};\nconst metaInput: React.CSSProperties = {\n  width: \"100%\",\n  padding: \"4px 6px\",\n  border: \"1px solid transparent\",\n  background: \"transparent\",\n  fontSize: 13,\n  color: \"var(--text)\",\n  outline: \"none\",\n  borderRadius: 4,\n};\nconst iconBtn: React.CSSProperties = {\n  background: \"transparent\",\n  border: \"none\",\n  cursor: \"pointer\",\n  padding: 4,\n  display: \"inline-flex\",\n  alignItems: \"center\",\n};"

> AGENT

All three clean. **Restart the backend** for the type update (no runtime change but keeps types aligned). Hard-reload dashboard. Reload field-app JS (Metro will pick it up — no APK rebuild).

**What's fixed:**

1. **Barcode re-scans now auto-resolve.** `replaceCanonicalProducts` was doing `DELETE FROM canonical_products` and the FK from `product_barcodes` (`ON DELETE CASCADE` with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`) wiped every learned barcode → product mapping on each 30-second sync. Changed to UPSERT + targeted cleanup, so learned barcodes persist.

2. **Scanned receipt now reflects in the order's Received column.** `OrdersScreen` was reading remote orders straight to UI state without writing them to local SQLite. `ReceivingScreen.findOpenItemByProductId()` returned `null`, so `addReceivedQty(...)` never ran and the receipt POST also lacked `order_item_id`. Added `upsertOrdersFromRemote(...)` (new) and wired it into both `OrdersScreen.load()` and the periodic `flushOnce()` + the `CatalogPicker.refresh()` so the local mirror stays current. Added `product_id` to the `RemoteOrderItem` type so the local cache can resolve by canonical product.

3. **Dashboard Orders tab — cleaner Excel-style layout.**
   - Collapsed header now leads with vendor (bigger), bill # + date as a subtitle, and a right-aligned **Received N / M** pair with a slim progress bar + status pill + delete icon. Much less ambiguous than the prior `N items · X/Y received` string.
   - Expanded view is two clean sections separated by a single border each:
     - **Bill meta** as a sheet-style label/value rows (Vendor | Bill # | Bill date), each row click-to-edit, "Save bill details" appears only when something changes.
     - **Items** as a single bordered table with a header row (Product | HSN | Qty | Rate | Pack | Received | ⌫). Edits are inline, auto-save on blur. The Received column shows `N / M` with the actual `N` in green when fully received. The "Add an item from catalog" row is the last `<tr>`, visually consistent with the data rows.

**After restart, the end-to-end loop should be:**
- Validate a bill → appears in Orders tab (collapsed; expand to inspect/edit).
- Guard scans an unknown barcode → CatalogPicker → picks Product X → ReceivingScreen → confirm. The local order_item received_qty increments AND the barcode→product mapping is written.
- Same guard re-scans the same barcode → goes straight to ReceivingScreen with Product X pre-resolved (no CatalogPicker).
- Open the Orders tab in the dashboard → the order's Received column shows the new totals.
- Open the Export tab → the new receipt is in the compliance log (now correctly populated because site_id is aligned and the order_item link exists).

Let me know which still misbehaves and I'll keep going.

  "old_string": "/**\n * Drop every learned alias for a site. Useful when the alias cache has\n * been poisoned by a prior run that auto-saved wrong mappings.\n */",
  "new_string": "export type CatalogSheetRow = {\n  canonical_name: string;\n  category: string | null;\n  unit: string;\n  pack_size: number;\n  last_price: number | null;\n  barcodes: string | null; // comma-separated\n  hsn_code: string | null;\n};\n\n/**\n * Snapshot of the catalog for the Google Sheet \"Catalog\" tab. Joins\n * canonical_products → product_barcodes (concatenated) and pulls the\n * most recent unit_rate from inventory_order_items as a price proxy\n * (canonical products don't carry a price column today).\n */\nexport async function listCatalogForSheet(siteId: string): Promise<CatalogSheetRow[]> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  const result = await db.execute({\n    sql: `\n      SELECT\n        cp.canonical_name,\n        cp.category,\n        cp.unit,\n        cp.pack_size,\n        cp.hsn_code,\n        (SELECT string_agg(pb.barcode, ', ')\n           FROM product_barcodes pb\n          WHERE pb.product_id = cp.product_id) AS barcodes,\n        (SELECT oi.unit_rate\n           FROM inventory_order_items oi\n           JOIN inventory_orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id\n          WHERE oi.product_id = cp.product_id AND o.site_id = ?\n          ORDER BY o.created_at DESC\n          LIMIT 1) AS last_price\n      FROM canonical_products cp\n      WHERE cp.site_id = ?\n      ORDER BY cp.canonical_name\n    `,\n    args: [siteId, siteId],\n  });\n  return result.rows as unknown as CatalogSheetRow[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Drop every learned alias for a site. Useful when the alias cache has\n * been poisoned by a prior run that auto-saved wrong mappings.\n */"
}

> AGENT

All green. **Restart `office-ops-engine`** then hard-reload the dashboard.

**What's new — Catalog tab in the Sheet:**

- New `Catalog` tab is auto-created with headers: `Product Name | Category | Unit | Unit Value | Price | Barcode | HSN`.
- Unlike Ordered/Received (which append rows over time), Catalog is a **snapshot** — it's wiped and rewritten so it always reflects the current canonical catalog.
- Rebuilt automatically after every:
  - bill validate (new products that get registered)
  - `POST /api/inventory/canonical-products` (admin's "New product" button)
- Manual refresh from the dashboard: Export tab → SheetConfigCard → "**Sync catalog**" button.
- Backend endpoint: `POST /api/inventory/sheet/sync-catalog`.

**Column details:**
- **Barcode** = comma-separated list of every barcode learned for that product (`product_barcodes` join). Empty if none have been scanned yet.
- **Price** = most recent `unit_rate` from any `inventory_order_items` row for that product (latest bill price). Empty if the product has never appeared on a bill.

If you'd rather have **Price** as an editable field on the canonical product itself (instead of a derived "latest bill price"), I'd add a `price` column to `canonical_products` and surface it in the New Product form. Just say the word.

> AGENT

Clean. Reload the field-app JS (Metro will pick it up).

**The actual bug:** the Receiving screen's primary "Add to Order" button doesn't write the receipt — it just adds the item to an in-memory `orderSession`. The session's `submitAll()` is the one that enqueues receipts, calls `addReceivedQty()`, and persists data. But:

1. `OrderSessionItem` only carried `barcode`, not `productId`. So when the receipt got enqueued, `product_id` was always null — the backend couldn't link to the canonical order item, and the barcode→product mapping was never learned.
2. The session looked up the order item via `findOpenItemByBarcode(item.barcode)` — but bills validated through the new flow create order items keyed by `product_id`, not by physical barcode. So that lookup always returned null and `addReceivedQty()` never ran.

**Fix:**

- `OrderSessionItem` now carries `productId`.
- `ReceivingScreen.addToSession()` forwards it from route params.
- `OrderSessionContext.submitAll()`:
  - Resolves the open order item by `productId` first (catalog flow), falling back to barcode (legacy).
  - Sends `product_id` in the receipt payload so the backend's compliance log + the dashboard's Received counter actually see this scan.
  - Calls `learnBarcode(barcode, productId)` AND enqueues the `learn_barcode` outbox row so the next scan of the same physical barcode auto-resolves without showing the CatalogPicker.

After reloading the field-app JS:
- Scan → catalog pick → "Add to Order" → finalize session (the OrderSession screen's submit) → the next scan of the same barcode goes straight to Receiving with the product pre-resolved, and the Orders tab's Received column reflects the new qty.

If you'd rather skip the OrderSession entirely and have the single "Confirm" button on Receiving write the receipt right away (like `persistStandalone` already does), I can flip the primary action — let me know.

> AGENT

Two more likely failure points:

1. **Local `order_items` may not be in SQLite when `submitAll()` runs** (the periodic sync hasn't fired yet). Then `findOpenItemByProductId` returns null → both client and server see `order_item_id: null` → server's `addReceivedQty` is skipped → the Received counter stays at 0 even though the receipt was recorded.
2. **The server only increments `received_qty` when `order_item_id` is sent.** It should also resolve it from `product_id` as a fallback.

Fix both.

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`.** Reload field-app JS (force a fresh bundle — shake → Reload).

**The new defenses, in layers — at least one should make it work:**

1. **CatalogPicker learns the barcode the moment the user picks a product.** No dependency on completing the receipt — the next scan auto-resolves even if they back out, cancel, or the order session never gets submitted.
2. **OrderSession.submitAll syncs orders first** so `findOpenItemByProductId` has fresh data before resolving the order link.
3. **Backend receipts route falls back to `findOpenItemByProductId(siteId, productId)`** when the client sends `product_id` but couldn't resolve `order_item_id`. The Received counter increments server-side regardless of the field-app's local cache state.
4. **Backend also auto-learns the barcode on receipt** whenever both `barcode` and `product_id` are present.

If after this it still doesn't work, the most useful next step is logs:
- Inside `CatalogPicker.pick` — `console.log` the `incomingBarcode` and `product.product_id` to confirm both are set when you tap a product.
- The backend's incoming receipt — paste the request body so I can see what the field-app actually sent (specifically whether `product_id` arrives).

Drop those and I'll trace the failing path directly.

> AGENT

Already wired. **Hard-reload the dashboard.**

**What changed:**

- **Canonical name field is now a full combobox.** Type any character → live-filters the entire catalog (not the static top-3 from the backend) with rank: exact > prefix > substring > category/HSN substring. Keyboard nav (↑/↓ + Enter) works; outside-click dismisses. Selecting a row auto-fills **canonical_name + category + unit + pack_size + hsn_code** from the catalog and flips the row to `use_existing` (mapped to catalog).
- **Catalog list is no longer cached per-row.** The combobox draws from a React-Query catalog query inside `BillUploadTab` with `staleTime: 0`, so newly-created products show up the next time you open the bill review.
- **"Category" field is now visible and editable** on each row (previously hidden). It's submitted in the validate payload so newly registered products land in the catalog with the right category.
- **The chip strip is gone.** A single small **"Did you mean: <closest match> · pack unit"** pill appears below the row only when the backend's top suggestion is meaningfully different from what's currently in the name field. Click it to accept (same auto-fill behaviour as a dropdown pick). When the spelling already matches or you've already mapped it, the pill stays hidden.

Smoke test:
1. Upload a bill with at least one item whose canonical match is in the catalog.
2. Click the name input → dropdown of catalog items appears immediately.
3. Type a few characters → list narrows.
4. Pick one → name/category/unit/pack/HSN auto-fill; the row becomes "Mapped to catalog".
5. Backspace the name → row reverts to "Will register as new"; the "Did you mean" pill reappears if the catalog still has a close match.

Catches\n *  typos like \"wagh bkri\" → \"wagh bakri\" without flooding the user\n *  with low-quality matches. */\nfunction similarity(a: string, b: string): number {\n  const la = a.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '');\n  const lb = b.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '');\n  if (la === lb) return 1;\n  if (la.length < 2 || lb.length < 2) return 0;\n  const bg = (s: string) => {\n    const out = new Set<string>();\n    for (let i = 0; i < s.length - 1; i++) out.add(s.slice(i, i + 2));\n    return out;\n  };\n  const A = bg(la);\n  const B = bg(lb);\n  let inter = 0;\n  for (const x of A) if (B.has(x)) inter++;\n  return (2 * inter) / (A.size + B.size);\n}\n\nexport function CatalogPickerScreen({ navigation, route }: Props) {\n  const { palette } = useTheme();\n  const incomingBarcode = route.params?.barcode;\n  const [products, setProducts] = useState<CanonicalProduct[]>([]);\n  const [openItemMap, setOpenItemMap] = useState<Record<string, OpenOrderItem>>({});\n  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);\n\n  const loadFromCache = useCallback(async () => {\n    const all = await listCanonicalProducts();\n    setProducts(all);\n\n    const db = await getDb();\n    const rows = await db.getAllAsync<OpenOrderItem>(\n      `SELECT oi.product_id, oi.expected_qty, oi.received_qty\n       FROM order_items oi\n       JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id\n       WHERE o.status = 'open' AND oi.product_id IS NOT NULL`,\n    );\n    const map: Record<string, OpenOrderItem> = {};\n    for (const r of rows) map[r.product_id] = r;\n    setOpenItemMap(map);\n    setLoading(false);\n  }, []);\n\n  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {\n    await Promise.all([syncCanonicalProducts(), syncOrders()]);\n    await loadFromCache();\n  }, [loadFromCache]);\n\n  useFocusEffect(\n    useCallback(() => {\n      void refresh();\n    }, [refresh]),\n  );\n\n  /** Build the dropdown list:\n   *   1. With no query — show items expected on open orders first, then\n   *      the rest, capped at MAX_VISIBLE.\n   *   2. With a query — rank by match strength (exact > prefix >\n   *      substring > category/HSN substring), capped at MAX_VISIBLE.\n   *   3. Always compute the best fuzzy near-miss separately for the\n   *      \"Did you mean…\" pill. */\n  const { visible, suggestion } = useMemo(() => {\n    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();\n    if (!q) {\n      const expected = products.filter((p) => openItemMap[p.product_id]);\n      const others = products.filter((p) => !openItemMap[p.product_id]);\n      return {\n        visible: [...expected, ...others].slice(0, MAX_VISIBLE),\n        suggestion: null as CanonicalProduct | null,\n      };\n    }\n\n    type Scored = { p: CanonicalProduct; score: number };\n    const scored: Scored[] = products.map((p) => {\n      const name = p.canonical_name.toLowerCase();\n      let score = 0;\n      if (name === q) score = 3;\n      else if (name.startsWith(q)) score = 2;\n      else if (name.includes(q)) score = 1;\n      else if ((p.category ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(q)) score = 0.5;\n      else if ((p.hsn_code ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(q)) score = 0.5;\n      return { p, score };\n    });\n\n    const exactMatches = scored.filter((x) => x.score > 0);\n    exactMatches.sort((a, b) => {\n      if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n      // prefer items expected on open orders, then alphabetical\n      const aExpected = openItemMap[a.p.product_id] ? 1 : 0;\n      const bExpected = openItemMap[b.p.product_id] ? 1 : 0;\n      if (bExpected !== aExpected) return bExpected - aExpected;\n      return a.p.canonical_name.localeCompare(b.p.canonical_name);\n    });\n\n    let suggestion: CanonicalProduct | null = null;\n    if (exactMatches.length === 0) {\n      let best: CanonicalProduct | null = null;\n      let bestScore = 0;\n      for (const p of products) {\n        const s = similarity(query, p.canonical_name);\n        if (s > bestScore) { bestScore = s; best = p; }\n      }\n      if (best && bestScore >= 0.35) suggestion = best;\n    }\n\n    return {\n      visible: exactMatches.slice(0, MAX_VISIBLE).map((x) => x.p),\n      suggestion,\n    };\n  }, [products, openItemMap, query]);\n\n  async function pick(product: CanonicalProduct) {\n    // Learn barcode → product the moment the guard picks, so a future\n    // scan auto-resolves even if they cancel the receipt downstream.\n    if (incomingBarcode) {\n      try {\n        await learnBarcode(incomingBarcode, product.product_id, 'scan');\n        await enqueue('learn_barcode', {\n          barcode: incomingBarcode,\n          product_id: product.product_id,\n        }).catch(() => {});\n      } catch {\n        // Non-fatal: the receipt flow has its own learning step.\n      }\n    }\n    const barcode = incomingBarcode ?? `catalog_${product.product_id}`;\n    navigation.replace('Receiving', {\n      barcode,\n      productId: product.product_id,\n      productName: product.canonical_name,\n      unit: product.unit,\n      packSize: product.pack_size,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <View style={[styles.safe, { backgroundColor: palette.background }]}>\n      <AppBar\n        title=\"Pick product\"\n        subtitle={`${products.length} item${products.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} in catalog`}\n        onBack={() => navigation.goBack()}\n        trailing={<IconButton Icon={RefreshCw} onPress={() => void refresh()} />}\n      />\n\n      <View style={{ padding: spacing.md }}>\n        <View\n          style={{\n            flexDirection: 'row',\n            alignItems: 'center',\n            gap: spacing.sm,\n            paddingHorizontal: spacing.md,\n            borderRadius: radius.md,\n            backgroundColor: palette.surfaceContainerLowest,\n            borderWidth: 1,\n            borderColor: palette.outlineVariant,\n          }}\n        >\n          <Search size={18} color={palette.onSurfaceVariant} strokeWidth={2.2} />\n          <TextInput\n            value={query}\n            onChangeText={setQuery}\n            placeholder=\"Type product name, category or HSN…\"\n            placeholderTextColor={palette.onSurfaceVariant}\n            style={{ flex: 1, paddingVertical: spacing.md, color: palette.onSurface, fontSize: 15 }}\n            autoCorrect={false}\n            autoCapitalize=\"none\"\n            autoFocus\n          />\n        </View>\n      </View>\n\n      {loading ? (\n        <View style={{ paddingHorizontal: spacing.md, gap: spacing.sm }}>\n          <Skeleton height={60} />\n          <Skeleton height={60} />\n          <Skeleton height={60} />\n        </View>\n      ) : (\n        <FlatList\n          data={visible}\n          keyExtractor={(p) => p.product_id}\n          keyboardShouldPersistTaps=\"handled\"\n          contentContainerStyle={{ paddingHorizontal: spacing.md, paddingBottom: spacing.xl * 2, gap: spacing.sm }}\n          renderItem={({ item: p }) => {\n            const oi = openItemMap[p.product_id];\n            return (\n              <Pressable onPress={() => { void pick(p); }}>\n                <Card>\n                  <View style={{ padding: spacing.md, flexDirection: 'row', justifyContent: 'space-between', alignItems: 'center', gap: spacing.md }}>\n                    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>\n                      <Text variant=\"titleMedium\">{p.canonical_name}</Text>\n                      <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', gap: spacing.sm, marginTop: 2, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>\n                        {p.category ? (\n                          <Text variant=\"labelMedium\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant}>{p.category}</Text>\n                        ) : null}\n                        {p.hsn_code ? (\n                          <Text variant=\"labelMedium\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant}>HSN {p.hsn_code}</Text>\n                        ) : null}\n                      </View>\n                    </View>\n                    <View style={{ alignItems: 'flex-end' }}>\n                      <Text variant=\"titleMedium\" color={palette.onSurface}>\n                        {p.pack_size} {p.unit}\n                      </Text>\n                      {oi && (\n                        <Text variant=\"labelMedium\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant}>\n                          {oi.received_qty}/{oi.expected_qty}\n                        </Text>\n                      )}\n                    </View>\n                  </View>\n                </Card>\n              </Pressable>\n            );\n          }}\n          ListEmptyComponent={\n            <Card>\n              <View style={{ padding: spacing.lg, alignItems: 'center', gap: spacing.sm }}>\n                <Text variant=\"bodyLarge\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant} style={{ textAlign: 'center' }}>\n                  No exact match.\n                </Text>\n                <Text variant=\"labelMedium\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant} style={{ textAlign: 'center' }}>\n                  Try fewer letters, refresh the catalog, or flag with a photo.\n                </Text>\n              </View>\n            </Card>\n          }\n          ListFooterComponent={\n            <View style={{ marginTop: spacing.lg, gap: spacing.sm }}>\n              {suggestion && (\n                <Pressable onPress={() => { void pick(suggestion); }}>\n                  <View\n                    style={{\n                      paddingVertical: spacing.sm,\n                      paddingHorizontal: spacing.md,\n                      borderWidth: 1,\n                      borderColor: palette.outlineVariant,\n                      borderRadius: 999,\n                      alignSelf: 'flex-start',\n                      flexDirection: 'row',\n                      alignItems: 'center',\n                      gap: spacing.xs,\n                    }}\n                  >\n                    <Text variant=\"labelMedium\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant}>Did you mean:</Text>\n                    <Text variant=\"labelLarge\" color={palette.onSurface}>{suggestion.canonical_name}</Text>\n                    <Text variant=\"labelMedium\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant}>\n                      · {suggestion.pack_size} {suggestion.unit}\n                    </Text>\n                  </View>\n                </Pressable>\n              )}\n              <Pressable onPress={() => navigation.goBack()}>\n                <Card>\n                  <View style={{ padding: spacing.md, flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: spacing.sm, justifyContent: 'center' }}>\n                    <Camera size={18} color={palette.onSurfaceVariant} strokeWidth={2.2} />\n                    <Text variant=\"labelLarge\" color={palette.onSurfaceVariant}>\n                      Not in this list? Flag with a photo\n                    </Text>\n                  </View>\n                </Pressable>\n              </View>\n            </View>\n          }\n        />\n      )}\n    </View>\n  );\n}\n\nconst styles = StyleSheet.create({\n  safe: { flex: 1 },\n});\n"
}

> AGENT

Clean. Reload field-app JS (Metro will pick it up).

**What changed in the field-app CatalogPicker:**

- **Single combined dropdown list.** No more "Expected from open orders" / "All products" sections. Items expected on open orders are still surfaced first (when the query is empty, or as a tiebreaker when sorted), but they're not in a separate visually-noisy section.
- **Live, ranked filtering of the full catalog.** Type → list narrows by: exact match > prefix > substring > category/HSN substring. Capped at 8 visible rows so the dropdown stays small instead of becoming a long scroll.
- **One closest-match pill at the bottom.** When no items match the typed text as a substring, the closest fuzzy match (bigram similarity ≥ 0.35) appears as a single rounded pill labeled "Did you mean: <name> · <pack> <unit>". Tap it to pick that product directly. No more multi-pill row.
- **Auto-fill on pick.** The pick flow already navigates to Receiving with `{ productId, productName, unit, packSize }` — these come straight from the canonical product, so unit and unit value are set automatically. The category lives server-side and is associated to the product via productId; no extra plumbing needed for the receipt.
- **Catalog stays fresh.** Refetched on every screen focus + RefreshCw button in the AppBar + the periodic `flushOnce` cycle. The "list cached once and forgotten" issue is gone; if a row is missing, hit Refresh once to force a sync.

If anything specific in the catalog still doesn't show up after refresh, paste the product name and I'll trace whether it's in the local SQLite, in the API response, or genuinely missing from the site's catalog.

Bind ids as literals (the\n  // list is small and ids are alphanumeric); a parameterised IN with\n  // dynamic length is painful in expo-sqlite.\n  const ids = products.map((p) => `'${String(p.product_id).replace(/'/g, \"''\")}'`).join(',');\n  await db.execAsync(`DELETE FROM canonical_products WHERE product_id NOT IN (${ids})`);\n}",
  "new_string": "/**\n * Replace the entire canonical product catalog with fresh data\n * from the backend. Used during full sync.\n *\n * IMPORTANT: do NOT `DELETE FROM canonical_products` first — there is a\n * cascading FK from `product_barcodes`, so a blanket delete blows away\n * every learned barcode → product mapping the guard has built up.\n * Instead we upsert each remote row, then delete the ones the remote\n * no longer knows about.\n *\n * Per-row try/catch: one bad payload row used to abort the whole loop,\n * which left the local cache silently missing items further down the\n * list. Now we count failures and surface them so they can be diagnosed.\n */\nexport async function replaceCanonicalProducts(\n  products: CanonicalProduct[],\n): Promise<{ ok: number; failed: number; firstError?: string }> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  let ok = 0;\n  let failed = 0;\n  let firstError: string | undefined;\n  for (const p of products) {\n    try {\n      // Coerce fields the local schema marks NOT NULL — the server should\n      // already enforce these, but a single bad row (e.g. unit migrated\n      // from null) shouldn't drop the rest of the catalog.\n      await upsertCanonicalProduct({\n        product_id: String(p.product_id),\n        canonical_name: String(p.canonical_name ?? ''),\n        category: p.category ?? null,\n        hsn_code: p.hsn_code ?? null,\n        unit: p.unit ?? 'pcs',\n        pack_size:\n          typeof p.pack_size === 'number' && Number.isFinite(p.pack_size)\n            ? p.pack_size\n            : 1,\n        updated_at: p.updated_at ?? Date.now(),\n      });\n      ok++;\n    } catch (err) {\n      failed++;\n      if (!firstError) firstError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n      // eslint-disable-next-line no-console\n      console.warn(`[catalog] upsert failed for ${p.product_id}:`, err);\n    }\n  }\n  if (products.length === 0) return { ok, failed, firstError }; // empty payload — keep what we have\n\n  // Drop products the remote no longer has. Bind ids as literals (the\n  // list is small and ids are alphanumeric); a parameterised IN with\n  // dynamic length is painful in expo-sqlite.\n  const ids = products.map((p) => `'${String(p.product_id).replace(/'/g, \"''\")}'`).join(',');\n  try {\n    await db.execAsync(`DELETE FROM canonical_products WHERE product_id NOT IN (${ids})`);\n  } catch (err) {\n    // eslint-disable-next-line no-console\n    console.warn('[catalog] stale-cleanup delete failed:', err);\n  }\n  return { ok, failed, firstError };\n}"
}

> AGENT

Reload Metro. Now the AppBar subtitle will tell us **what's actually happening**:

- `"39 items in catalog"` — local cache matches remote; "fortune…" is genuinely in there. Try a shorter search like just `fort`.
- `"38 cached · sync 38/39"` — remote returned 39 but one row failed to write locally. Open the Metro console, you'll see `[catalog] upsert failed for prod_…: <reason>` from the new logs. That's the "fortune…" row, almost certainly with bad/null fields.
- `"X cached · sync error"` — the fetch itself failed (auth, network). Console log will name the error.
- `"38 items in catalog"` and the user expects 39 — the dashboard's "fortune…" was never actually saved as a canonical product. **Common cause:** seeing the item only in the bill-upload review screen ≠ it's in the catalog. It only joins the catalog after you click **Validate & save (N)**. Open the dashboard's **Catalog** tab and search there; if it isn't in that table, it was never validated and the field-app correctly doesn't have it.

Tell me which of the four subtitles you see and I'll do the next step. The fixes shipped in this round also matter regardless:

- Per-item try/catch in `replaceCanonicalProducts` — one bad row no longer drops the rest.
- `console.warn` instead of swallowing every error.
- `getLastCatalogSync()` exposes the count so the picker shows the discrepancy without you having to look at logs.
- Defensive coercion (`unit ?? 'pcs'`, finite `pack_size`) when writing each row, so a NOT NULL constraint can no longer torpedo an entire sync.

For the second part — "selecting a catalog item doesn't update category/unit/unit value" — that's only true on screens that don't *display* those fields. The dashboard's bill-review row does (Category input + Unit select + Pack size input, all auto-filled by `acceptCatalog`). The field-app's Receiving screen only displays `pack_size unit` on the right of the product name and doesn't display category at all. If you want category visible there too, say so and I'll add the row. Otherwise, the data is correct — it's keyed to the product via `product_id` server-side.

> AGENT

Almost certainly not. Which "new product page" do you mean?

- **Dashboard → Catalog tab → "New product" form:** Vite hot-reload only. If recent edits aren't visible, hard-reload the tab (Cmd+Shift+R) — sometimes the dev server holds onto a stale chunk. No build needed.
- **Field-app:** every change we've made this session is pure JS/TS — Metro hot-reload picks it up. Shake the device → **Reload**. The APK only needs rebuilding when `app.json` plugins or a native `react-native-*` library changes (none of that this session).

So the steps in order:
1. Save the file (the editor should already have).

1	import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';
2	import { KnownProduct, listKnownProducts } from '../../../db/catalog';
3	import { buildNameIndex, rankByName, type NameIndexEntry } from './nameMatch';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Returns up to `limit` catalog products that fuzzy-match `query`.
7	 * Catalog is loaded once on first use and re-loaded whenever the
8	 * returned `reload()` is called (e.g. after a successful registration).
9	 *
10	 * Matching layers (cheapest first, all client-side):
11	 *   - normalized substring / prefix match
12	 *   - Soundex-style phonetic key match (so "ghee" finds "ghi", and
13	 *     a Hindi input like "घी" — transliterated to "ghi" — also hits)
14	 *   - Levenshtein distance fallback for typos ("watrmilan" → "Watermelon")
15	 *
16	 * Zero network calls, no extra deps.
17	 */
18	export function useCatalogSuggest(query: string, limit = 3) {
19	  const [catalog, setCatalog] = useState<KnownProduct[]>([]);
20	
21	  const reload = useMemo(
22	    () => async () => {
23	      const rows = await listKnownProducts();
24	      setCatalog(rows);
25	    },
26	    [],
27	  );
28	
29	  useEffect(() => {
30	    reload().catch(() => {});
31	  }, [reload]);
32	
33	  const index = useMemo<NameIndexEntry<KnownProduct>[]>(
34	    () => buildNameIndex(catalog, (p) => p.name ?? ''),
35	    [catalog],
36	  );
37	
38	  const suggestions = useMemo<KnownProduct[]>(() => {
39	    const q = query.trim();
40	    if (q.length < 2 || index.length === 0) return [];
41	    return rankByName(index, q, limit).map((r) => r.item);
42	  }, [index, query, limit]);
43	
44	  return { suggestions, reload };
45	}
46

> AGENT

Found it. The "new product page" is `RegisterProductScreen`, reached when the scanner sees an unknown barcode. It uses an old hook `useCatalogSuggest` that pulls from the **legacy local products table + stock cache** — *not* the admin-created canonical catalog. That's why the dashboard's products never show up there. Also the suggestion UI is a horizontal pill row, not a dropdown.

Let me rewrite it:
- New hook reading from `canonical_products` (the admin catalog).
- Dropdown panel below the name input as you type.
- Single "Did you mean" pill below the input for typo correction.
- Picking auto-fills name + category + unit + pack_size and remembers values outside the predefined chip lists.
- Save now maps the scanned barcode → canonical product (so next scan auto-resolves to Receiving).

  "content": "import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';\nimport { CanonicalProduct, listCanonicalProducts } from '../../../db/catalog';\n\n/** Dice (bigram) similarity — surfaces a single \"did you mean…\" pick\n *  when nothing matches as a substring. */\nfunction similarity(a: string, b: string): number {\n  const la = a.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '');\n  const lb = b.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '');\n  if (la === lb) return 1;\n  if (la.length < 2 || lb.length < 2) return 0;\n  const bg = (s: string) => {\n    const out = new Set<string>();\n    for (let i = 0; i < s.length - 1; i++) out.add(s.slice(i, i + 2));\n    return out;\n  };\n  const A = bg(la);\n  const B = bg(lb);\n  let inter = 0;\n  for (const x of A) if (B.has(x)) inter++;\n  return (2 * inter) / (A.size + B.size);\n}\n\n/**\n * Returns substring/prefix matches against the admin-curated canonical\n * catalog, plus a single closest fuzzy match for typo correction.\n *\n *  - `matches`    — ranked exact/prefix/substring hits (for the dropdown)\n *  - `suggestion` — best Dice-similarity hit (≥ 0.35) ONLY when there\n *                   are no substring matches, for the \"Did you mean…\" pill\n *  - `catalog`    — the full local cache, exposed so the caller can show\n *                   \"N items in catalog\" diagnostics\n *  - `reload()`   — re-reads from SQLite (call after a sync)\n */\nexport function useCanonicalSuggest(query: string) {\n  const [catalog, setCatalog] = useState<CanonicalProduct[]>([]);\n\n  const reload = useMemo(\n    () => async () => {\n      const rows = await listCanonicalProducts();\n      setCatalog(rows);\n    },\n    [],\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    reload().catch(() => {});\n  }, [reload]);\n\n  const { matches, suggestion } = useMemo(() => {\n    const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();\n    if (!q) {\n      return {\n        matches: [...catalog].sort((a, b) => a.canonical_name.localeCompare(b.canonical_name)),\n        suggestion: null as CanonicalProduct | null,\n      };\n    }\n\n    type Scored = { p: CanonicalProduct; score: number };\n    const scored: Scored[] = catalog.map((p) => {\n      const name = p.canonical_name.toLowerCase();\n      let score = 0;\n      if (name === q) score = 3;\n      else if (name.startsWith(q)) score = 2;\n      else if (name.includes(q)) score = 1;\n      else if ((p.category ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(q)) score = 0.5;\n      else if ((p.hsn_code ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(q)) score = 0.5;\n      return { p, score };\n    });\n    const hits = scored\n      .filter((x) => x.score > 0)\n      .sort((a, b) => {\n        if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n        return a.p.canonical_name.localeCompare(b.p.canonical_name);\n      })\n      .map((x) => x.p);\n\n    let bestSuggestion: CanonicalProduct | null = null;\n    if (hits.length === 0) {\n      let best: CanonicalProduct | null = null;\n      let bestScore = 0;\n      for (const p of catalog) {\n        const s = similarity(query, p.canonical_name);\n        if (s > bestScore) { bestScore = s; best = p; }\n      }\n      if (best && bestScore >= 0.35) bestSuggestion = best;\n    }\n\n    return { matches: hits, suggestion: bestSuggestion };\n  }, [catalog, query]);\n\n  return { matches, suggestion, catalog, reload };\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Clean. Reload Metro (`r` or shake → Reload).

**What's now in `RegisterProductScreen` (the page you land on for an unknown barcode):**

- **Suggestions source = canonical catalog.** The new `useCanonicalSuggest` hook reads from local `canonical_products` (the admin-curated table, populated by the dashboard's catalog tab + bill validate flow). The old hook was reading from a different legacy table — that's why the dashboard's products never showed up here.
- **Dropdown panel, not a pill row.** As you type into the name field, a single bordered list of catalog matches drops down underneath. Tap to pick; the list collapses.
- **"Did you mean: <name>" pill** appears below the input only when there are no substring matches AND there's a close fuzzy hit (Dice similarity ≥ 0.35). One pill, not many.
- **Auto-fill on pick.** Selecting a row sets the name, category, unit and pack size to the catalog values. If the picked product's category or unit isn't in the default chip lists (e.g. `g`, `ml`, or a brand-specific category), the chip is added dynamically so you can see what was applied.
- **Save behaviour now branches:**
  - **Picked from catalog** → calls `learnBarcode(barcode → product_id)` locally, enqueues `learn_barcode` to the backend, and navigates to Receiving with the canonical product details. Next scan of this barcode goes straight to Receiving with no picker. Button label changes to **"Link to catalog & continue"**.
  - **Free-typed name** → creates a new local product as before, button stays as "Save and continue".
- **AppBar subtitle now shows sync diagnostics.** Will display `"38 cached · sync 38/39"` etc. if the local cache lags the server, so we can spot the discrepancy without console logs.
- **Pull to refresh.** Refresh icon in the AppBar + auto-sync on every focus + listens to `useFocusEffect`. The list now stays in sync with what the dashboard creates.

Test path:
1. From the dashboard, create a product like "Fortune Kachi Ghani Mustard Oil 910g" with category `Grocery`, unit `g`, pack 910.
2. In the field-app, scan any unknown barcode → land on this screen.
3. Type `fortune` → the dropdown shows the product.
4. Tap it → name, category, unit (`g`), pack size (910) all auto-fill. A green "✓ Mapped to catalog" message appears.
5. Tap **Link to catalog & continue** → goes to Receiving with the right product mapped.
6. Re-scan the same barcode → goes directly to Receiving with the product pre-resolved, no picker shown.

> AGENT

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`**; hard-reload the dashboard.

**What's done:**

1. **Unit + Pack are now editable in the Orders item table.** Two new columns: `Pack` (number input) and `Unit` (select with `pcs / kg / g / l / ml / pack`, plus any custom unit the product already uses). Editing either, then blurring the field, PATCHes the underlying canonical product (new endpoint `PATCH /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id`). Disabled with reduced opacity if the order item isn't linked to a catalog product (legacy rows). Catalog tab refresh triggers automatically, so the Sheet's Catalog tab updates too.

2. **Received column reworked.** Header changed to `Total qty | … | Received`. The Received cell now reads `**N** of M` (received qty bold on the left, expected qty muted), not `N / M`. Color: muted gray when nothing received, green when received ≥ expected, default otherwise. Much harder to misread when both numbers are multi-digit.

3. **"Sync catalog" button is gone.** The Catalog tab in the Sheet was already rebuilt automatically on:
   - bill validate (new canonical products),
   - admin "New product" form,
   - canonical product PATCH (the new edit path above),
   - and **now field registrations** (see #4).
   The card description was updated to reflect this; no more button.

4. **Field-app manual registrations now flow everywhere.** Backend's `POST /api/inventory/products` (called when a guard types a name on the RegisterProductScreen) used to write only to the legacy `inventory_products` table — invisible to the dashboard. Now it also:
   - upserts a `canonical_products` row using the guard's `name / category / unit / pack_size`,
   - calls `learnBarcode(barcode → product_id)` server-side so future scans auto-resolve,
   - kicks the Catalog Sheet sync.
   `created_by` is set to `field:<guard_name>` so admins can see at a glance which entries came from the floor versus from a validated bill.

End-to-end test:
- Guard scans an unknown barcode → enters "Maggi 70g" / Grocery / g / 70 → saves.
- Refresh dashboard → Catalog tab shows "Maggi 70g" with creator `field:<guard>`.
- Sheet's Catalog tab also has the row (with the barcode joined in via product_barcodes).
- Scan the same barcode again → goes straight to Receiving, no picker.

> AGENT

Found the real bug — and it's a classic JS gotcha. Postgres returns `NUMERIC` columns as **strings** through the pg driver. The OrderCard's `reduce((s, i) => s + i.expected_qty, 0)` then does `0 + "5"` → `"05"`, then `"05" + "3"` → `"053"`, and you end up with a 38-character string of concatenated digits. The TypeScript type lied (`number`) but the runtime value was a string.

Math.min(100, Math.round((totalReceived / totalExpected) * 100)) : 0;",
  "new_string": "function OrderCard({ order, onChange, onDelete }: { order: OrderFull; onChange: () => void; onDelete: () => void }) {\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n  // Postgres NUMERIC values come back through the pg driver as STRINGS, not\n  // numbers — adding them with `+` would silently concatenate (\"0\" + \"5\" =\n  // \"05\", then \"05\" + \"3\" = \"053\"…) and we'd display a 40-digit garbage\n  // value. Coerce explicitly here and everywhere we add or compare these.\n  const totalExpected = order.items.reduce((s, i) => s + (Number(i.expected_qty) || 0), 0);\n  const totalReceived = order.items.reduce((s, i) => s + (Number(i.received_qty) || 0), 0);\n  const progressPct = totalExpected > 0 ? Math.min(100, Math.round((totalReceived / totalExpected) * 100)) : 0;"
}

> AGENT

Dashboard clean. Hard-reload the browser tab.

**What changed:**

- **Root cause of the long-digit display** was a JavaScript quirk in `OrderCard`. The Postgres pg driver returns `NUMERIC` columns as strings, so `[0, "5", "3"].reduce((s, i) => s + i, 0)` becomes `0 + "5"` → `"05"`, then `"05" + "3"` → `"053"`. With dozens of items each contributing several digits, you end up with the 38-character horror you saw.
- **Fix:** every place that sums or compares an item's qty/received now does `Number(...)`. `OrderCard`'s totals are coerced. `OrderItemRow` normalises `expected_qty`, `received_qty`, `unit_rate`, `pack_size` to numbers at the top of the component and uses those typed variables for state init, dirty checks, color logic, and display.
- The collapsed card's right-side block will now read correctly as `Received: 12 / 20` (with a properly-sized progress bar), and the expanded row's Received cell shows the actual scalar like `**12** of 20`.

If you still see a giant number after reload, that means the DB itself has a polluted value (it'd take a real `received_qty = '0521…'` row in `inventory_order_items`). If so, run:

```sql
SELECT id, product_name, expected_qty, received_qty
FROM inventory_order_items
WHERE length(received_qty::text) > 10
   OR length(expected_qty::text) > 10;
```

and we'll clean those rows. But I'd bet the reload alone fixes what you're seeing — the bad-looking values were only in the dashboard's reduced-totals view.

> DEVELOPER

what I was thinking, is that an item usually have a fixed barcode, and different vendors can name it differently, like an item with barcode 123455678 can be named as Refined oil, cooking oil, fortune oil etc, but the barcode will remain same. the challenge here, is that suppose we order from different vendors the same thing, and the naming scheme is different, so the matching will be an issue, what I was thinking is that allow people to pick names from the order list but internally we will append that name with the barcode. but then scanning that barcode, what name we will show if a barcode has too many names. do you have any suggestion on this, a better idea?

> AGENT

Good question — you're already 90% there. The cleanest mental model is to **separate identity from display**.

**Identity (immutable):** the barcode. One physical product = one identity. Don't try to encode vendor names into it.

**Display (one-and-only):** the `canonical_products.canonical_name`. This is the name everyone sees, picks, and reads on receipts. It's admin-curated and **single** — never "many names per barcode" in the UI. If five vendors call the same product five different things, you still display it as one name.

**Vendor variants (history):** the `product_aliases` table. Each vendor's spelling lives here as `raw_name → product_id`. These are matching keys, not display values. They never appear on the scanner or receipt — only in admin tools.

Concretely:

- When **scanning at the gate**: `barcode → product_barcodes → canonical_product → canonical_name`. Show that one name. (Optional UX: a small "Also known as: 3 vendor names" link that expands for context, but rarely needed.)
- When **validating a bill**: matching pipeline runs (exact → alias → HSN-fuzzy → LLM). Admin sees a suggestion: "this bill's *Refined Cooking Oil* looks like *Fortune Refined Oil 910g* — map?" One click, alias saved, done. Future bills auto-resolve.
- When **registering a new catalog product**: admin picks the most universally recognizable name (brand + descriptor + size, e.g. "Fortune Refined Oil 910g"). That's what guards see forever.
- The barcode itself is the identity key. If the same product comes in two different cartons with different barcodes (rare — usually case vs. unit pack), `product_barcodes` already supports many-to-one, so both barcodes point to the same canonical product.

**Why not append vendor names to the barcode internally:**
Concatenating creates a brittle composite key (you have to canonicalize "Refined Oil" vs "REFINED OIL" vs "Refined-Oil"). The natural many-to-one (aliases → product) is the same idea expressed cleanly in a join table. You already have it.

**One concrete improvement worth doing:**
Promote the canonical product's barcode list to be a first-class column on the dashboard's Catalog tab (you can see what barcodes have been learned at a glance), and show a small "Aliases (N)" expander on each canonical product so admins can audit what vendor names have been folded in. Optional, but it makes the model legible.

Net: **one barcode → one canonical product → one display name → many vendor aliases (hidden)**. That's the cleanest model and it's what we've already built; you don't need to invent a new abstraction. Want me to add the "view aliases" expander to the Catalog tab so you can poke at the relationships and feel confident?

What we will do it is that we will have standard name for the items and then the calling name or bill name, which can be many for a single standard product. so one thing that will not change is the barcode and the standard name, only the calling name or bill name(you decide what type of naming it is, canonical?) can be many, and we will store that. so when a bill is scanned, all the names will be compared with the billing names available, but we will show in the list the standard name and the bill name, and recommend the standard name if we are not 100% sure, if we have 100% match we will auto fill the standard name section. and this flow will be in the field-app as well. when a barcode is scanned, we know the standard name, and that barcode is mapped to that standard name, but in that day's bill the billing name is mapped with standard name, so even though when a barcode is scanned we will show the standard name to the person scanning, but the system will update the order/devlivery section of the bill name that it has been received. > AGENT

That model is exactly what's already in the schema — you've just named the pieces better. Here's the mapping:

| Your term | What it is in code |
|---|---|
| **Standard name** | `canonical_products.canonical_name` (one per product, admin-curated) |
| **Bill name / calling name** | `product_aliases.raw_name` (many per product, accumulated from bills) |
| **Barcode** | `product_barcodes.barcode → product_id` (one or more barcodes per standard product) |

The flow you're describing is what the system already does:

- **Bill upload → match:** Extract each bill line → check exact-name → check alias cache (`product_aliases`) → if a previously-seen vendor name hits, auto-map to the standard. Lower-confidence hits surface as "Did you mean…" for admin to confirm. On Validate, the bill_item_name gets saved as a new alias if it wasn't already → so next time the same vendor writes it the same way, it auto-resolves.
- **Gate scan:** `barcode → product_barcodes → canonical_product → canonical_name`. Guard always sees the standard name. The order item the scan increments is keyed by `product_id`, not by bill name. So if the bill said "Masala Noodles" and that line was mapped to the standard "Maggi Noodles 100g", scanning the barcode still increments that specific bill line.
- **Order detail (dashboard):** `inventory_order_items` already stores both — `product_name` is the standard, `bill_item_name` preserves the verbatim bill text for the audit trail.

Two **small** UI changes worth doing to surface the model as clearly as you're describing:

1. **Rename labels.** "Canonical name" → **"Standard name"** in every dashboard form/header. "Suggestions" → "Standard names". Keep `canonical_*` as the internal column name; just change the visible labels.
2. **Show bill name underneath standard name** in the Orders tab's item table:
   ```
   Maggi Noodles 100g                     [Pack] [Unit] [Qty] [Received]
   from bill: "Masala Noodles"
   ```
   So when an admin opens an order they see both — what the standard is, and what this vendor called it. Same in the Export tab.

Want me to ship those two changes? They're small (label rewrites + a one-line subtitle under the product name in the Orders/Export tables) and they make the model self-explanatory. The bill-match pipeline and gate-scan resolution don't need any logic changes — they're already doing what you described.

233	  scanned_at: string;

251	
252	export async function getComplianceLogForReceipt(
253	  siteId: string,
254	  receiptId: string,
255	): Promise<ComplianceLogRow | null> {
256	  const db = await getDb();
257	  const result = await db.execute({
258	    sql: `
259	      SELECT
260	        r.scanned_at,
261	        to_char(r.scanned_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS date,
262	        io.vendor AS vendor,
263	        io.bill_number AS bill_number,
264	        COALESCE(r.product_id, oi.product_id) AS product_id,
265	        COALESCE(cp.canonical_name, r.product_name) AS product_name,
266	        cp.category AS category,
267	        COALESCE(cp.hsn_code, oi.hsn_code) AS hsn_code,
268	        cp.unit AS unit,
269	        cp.pack_size AS pack_size,
270	        r.qty AS qty_received,
271	        oi.expected_qty AS expected_qty,
272	        oi.unit_rate AS unit_rate,
273	        (r.qty * COALESCE(oi.unit_rate, 0)) AS line_value,
274	        r.expiry_date AS expiry_date,
275	        COALESCE(g.name, r.guard_id) AS received_by,
276	        CASE
277	          WHEN oi.expected_qty IS NOT NULL AND r.qty <> oi.expected_qty THEN 'MISMATCH'
278	          ELSE 'OK'
279	        END AS status
280	      FROM inventory_receipts r
281	      LEFT JOIN inventory_order_items oi ON oi.id = r.order_item_id
282	      LEFT JOIN inventory_orders io ON io.id = r.order_id
283	      LEFT JOIN canonical_products cp ON cp.product_id = COALESCE(r.product_id, oi.product_id)
284	      LEFT JOIN guards g ON g.id = r.guard_id
285	      WHERE r.id = ? AND r.site_id = ?
286	      LIMIT 1
287	    `,
288	    args: [receiptId, siteId],
289	  });
290	  const row = (result.rows[0] as unknown as ComplianceLogRow | undefined) ?? null;
291	  return row;
292	}

302	  if (fromDate) { conds.push('r.scanned_at >= ?'); args.push(fromDate); }

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`** (so the compliance SQL returns the new `bill_item_name` column). Hard-reload the dashboard.

**What changed:**

- **Label rename**: every user-facing "Canonical name" → **"Standard name"** in the dashboard. Includes the bill upload review form, the Catalog tab form + table header, and the confirm-dialog text on "Clear learned aliases". The intro paragraph and the Sheet description card now say "standard product catalog" / "every standard product". Internal column/API names (`canonical_*`) stay unchanged so nothing else has to move.
- **Bill name shown alongside Standard name** in two places:
  - **Orders tab**, every expanded item row: when the standard name differs from what the vendor wrote, you see `from bill: "Masala Noodles"` under the product input.
  - **Export tab**, every receipt row: same `from bill: "…"` subtitle under the product name. If they match (or no bill name), the subtitle stays hidden so you're not flooded with redundant lines.

The model is now legible end-to-end: the **standard name** is what guards see and what shows up as the canonical row everywhere; the **bill name** is the vendor's spelling, kept as an alias for matching and shown alongside the standard name where useful for context.

> AGENT

That's a foreign-key from `inventory_receipts.order_id` to `inventory_orders.id` without `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Once a receipt has been scanned against an order, Postgres refuses the order delete.

Fix on both sides: (a) ALTER the FK to `ON DELETE SET NULL` so receipts get detached but kept as audit history, and (b) make the delete handler explicitly null out the receipt links first so older deployments work too.

> AGENT

Clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`** — the migration block will run and relax the FKs.

**Two-layer fix:**

1. **Schema migration on startup** (`postgres-schema.ts`) — drops the strict FKs and re-creates them with `ON DELETE SET NULL` on:
   - `inventory_receipts.order_id`
   - `inventory_receipts.order_item_id`
   - `inventory_mismatch_flags.order_item_id`
   - `inventory_mismatch_flags.receipt_id`
   
   Wrapped in a `DO $$ … EXCEPTION` block so first-time installs (where the constraint name may differ or not exist) don't abort. Result: deleting an order detaches receipts but keeps them in the audit log.

2. **App-level null-out in `deleteOrder`** — before the `DELETE FROM inventory_orders`, the function explicitly NULLs `order_id` / `order_item_id` on all linked receipts and mismatch flags. So even if the migration hasn't run yet (older deploys), the delete succeeds.

After restart, deleting the second and third duplicate orders works. The receipts that were scanned against them stay in the system — they show up in the Export tab without a vendor/bill link (since the order is gone), which is correct: the scan happened, it's recorded, but it's no longer tied to a removed duplicate order.

92	  checkoutTime?: string | null;
93	  approvalStatus: string;
94	}): string {
95	  if (record.currentlyInside && record.checkinTime) {
96	    return `Inside since ${formatShortDateTimeInIST(record.checkinTime)}`;
97	  }
98	  if (record.checkoutTime) {
99	    return `Exited at ${formatShortDateTimeInIST(record.checkoutTime)}`;
100	  }
101	  return `Status: ${record.approvalStatus}`;
102	}

135	function getSOPStatusSymbol(status: "pending" | "completed"): string {
136	  return status === "completed" ? "☑" : "☐";
137	}

139	export function buildSOPKeyboard(
140	  dateStr: string,
141	  sops: SOPTask[],
142	): TelegramBot.InlineKeyboardButton[][] {
143	  return sops.map((sop) => [
144	    {
145	      text: `${getSOPStatusSymbol(sop.status)} ${sop.task_name}`,
146	      callback_data: `sop_toggle:${dateStr}:${sop.id}`,
147	    },
148	  ]);

150	
151	export function buildSOPChecklistText(
152	  dateStr: string,
153	  sops: SOPTask[],
154	  options?: { lastUpdatedBy?: string },
155	): string {
156	  const completedCount = sops.filter(
157	    (sop) => sop.status === "completed",
158	  ).length;
159	  const pendingCount = sops.length - completedCount;
160	
161	  const lines = [
162	    `*Daily SOP Checklist* (${dateStr})`,
163	    `Completed: ${completedCount}/${sops.length}`,
164	    `Pending: ${pendingCount}`,
165	  ];
166	
167	  if (options?.lastUpdatedBy) {
168	    lines.push(`Last updated by: ${options.lastUpdatedBy}`);
169	  }
170	
171	  lines.push("", "Select a task to update its status.");
172	  return lines.join("\n");
173	}
174	
175	function buildSOPStatsText(stats: DailySOPStats): string {
176	  const lines = [
177	    `*Daily SOP Stats* (${stats.date})`,
178	    `Completion: ${stats.completedTasks}/${stats.totalTasks} (${stats.completionRate}%)`,
179	    `Pending: ${stats.pendingTasks}`,
180	  ];
181	
182	  if (stats.byAssignee.length > 0) {
183	    lines.push("", "*By Assignee*");
184	    for (const group of stats.byAssignee) {
185	      lines.push(
186	        `- ${group.assignee}: ${group.completedTasks}/${group.totalTasks} completed`,
187	      );
188	    }
189	  }
190	
191	  if (stats.completedBy.length > 0) {
192	    lines.push("", "*Completed By*");
193	    for (const group of stats.completedBy) {
194	      lines.push(`- ${group.staffName}: ${group.completedTasks} task(s)`);
195	    }
196	  }
197	
198	  if (stats.totalTasks === 0) {
199	    lines.push("", "No SOP tasks exist for this date.");
200	  }
201	
202	  return lines.join("\n");
203	}

226	export async function sendSOPChecklistToStaff(
227	  dateStr: string,
228	  sops: SOPTask[],
229	  excludeChatId?: number,
230	): Promise<{ sent: number; failed: number }> {
231	  const bot = getBot();
232	  const staffIds = [...new Set(tgConfig.sopStaffIds())].filter(
233	    (staffId) => staffId !== excludeChatId,
234	  );
235	
236	  let sent = 0;
237	  let failed = 0;
238	
239	  for (const staffId of staffIds) {
240	    try {
241	      await bot.sendMessage(staffId, buildSOPChecklistText(dateStr, sops), {
242	        parse_mode: "Markdown",
243	        reply_markup: {
244	          inline_keyboard: buildSOPKeyboard(dateStr, sops),
245	        },
246	      });
247	      sent += 1;
248	    } catch (error) {
249	      failed += 1;
250	      logWarn(
251	        `Failed to send SOP checklist to staff chat ${staffId}: ${getErrorMessage(error)}`,
252	      );
253	    }
254	  }
255	
256	  return { sent, failed };
257	}

284	
285	export async function handleCommand(msg: TelegramBot.Message, command: string): Promise<void> {
286	  const parts = command.trim().split(/\s+/);
287	  const cmd = parts[0]?.split("@")[0] ?? "";
288	  const args = parts.slice(1);
289	  logInfo(`Handling command ${cmd}`);
290	
291	  switch (cmd) {
292	    case "/summary": {
293	      const bot = getBot();
294	      await bot.sendChatAction(msg.chat.id, "typing");
295	
296	      const workflow = mastra.getWorkflow("dailySummaryWorkflow");
297	      if (!workflow) {
298	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, "⚠️ Summary workflow not available.");
299	        return;
300	      }
301	
302	      const run = await workflow.createRun();
303	      const result = await run.start({
304	        inputData: { triggerType: "manual" },
305	      });
306	
307	      const step = Object.values(result.steps).pop();
308	      if (step?.status === "success") {
309	        const output = step.output as Record<string, unknown>;
310	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, output.formattedReport as string, {
311	          parseMode: "Markdown",
312	        });
313	      } else {
314	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, "⚠️ Failed to generate summary.");
315	      }
316	      break;
317	    }
318	
319	    case "/sop": {
320	      // /sop trigger [shift] — manual trigger from config
321	      if (args[0] === "trigger") {
322	        const shift = args[1] || undefined;
323	        const dateStr = getCurrentISTDate();
324	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `⏳ Creating SOPs from config for ${dateStr}${shift ? ` (shift: ${shift})` : ''}...`);
325	
326	        try {
327	          const result = await createDailySOPsFromConfig(dateStr, shift);
328	          const lines = [`✅ *SOP Trigger Complete*`, `Created: ${result.created} tasks`, "", "*Assignments:*"];
329	          for (const a of result.assignments) {
330	            lines.push(`• ${a}`);
331	          }
332	          await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, lines.join("\n"), { parseMode: "Markdown" });
333	
334	          // Show the checklist if tasks were created
335	          if (result.created > 0) {
336	            const sops = await getSOPTasks(dateStr);
337	            const bot = getBot();
338	            await bot.sendMessage(msg.chat.id, buildSOPChecklistText(dateStr, sops), {
339	              parse_mode: "Markdown",
340	              reply_markup: {
341	                inline_keyboard: buildSOPKeyboard(dateStr, sops),
342	              },
343	            });
344	
345	            const staffDelivery = await sendSOPChecklistToStaff(dateStr, sops, msg.chat.id);
346	            if (staffDelivery.sent > 0) {
347	              await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `📨 SOP checklist forwarded to ${staffDelivery.sent} staff chat(s).`);
348	            }
349	          }
350	        } catch (error) {
351	          await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `❌ SOP trigger failed: ${getErrorMessage(error)}`);
352	        }
353	        break;
354	      }
355	
356	      // Default: /sop [date] — original behavior
357	      const dateStr = resolveSOPDate(args[0]);
358	      await createDailySOPs(dateStr);
359	      const sops = await getSOPTasks(dateStr);
360	
361	      const bot = getBot();
362	
363	      await bot.sendMessage(msg.chat.id, buildSOPChecklistText(dateStr, sops), {
364	        parse_mode: "Markdown",
365	        reply_markup: {
366	          inline_keyboard: buildSOPKeyboard(dateStr, sops),
367	        },
368	      });
369	
370	      const staffDelivery = await sendSOPChecklistToStaff(
371	        dateStr,
372	        sops,
373	        msg.chat.id,
374	      );
375	      if (staffDelivery.sent > 0 || staffDelivery.failed > 0) {
376	        const parts = [
377	          `📨 SOP checklist forwarded to ${staffDelivery.sent} staff chat(s).`,
378	        ];
379	        if (staffDelivery.failed > 0) {
380	          parts.push(`${staffDelivery.failed} delivery attempt(s) failed.`);
381	        }
382	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, parts.join(" "));
383	      }
384	
385	      break;
386	    }
387	
388	    case "/sopstats": {
389	      const dateStr = resolveSOPDate(args[0]);
390	      const stats = await getSOPStats(dateStr);
391	      await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, buildSOPStatsText(stats), {
392	        parseMode: "Markdown",
393	      });
394	      break;
395	    }
396	
397	    case "/visitors": {
398	      const records = await queryVisitorManagementRecords({
399	        scope: "today",
400	        date: getCurrentISTDate(),
401	        limit: 20,
402	      });
403	      if (records.length === 0) {
404	        await sendMessage(
405	          msg.chat.id,
406	          "👥 *Today's Visitors*\n\nNo visitor activity is recorded in the live visitor management system today.",
407	          { parseMode: "Markdown" },
408	        );
409	        break;
410	      }
411	
412	      const lines = records.map((record, index) => {
413	        const parts = [
414	          `${index + 1}. *${record.visitorName}*`,
415	          formatVisitorManagementStatus(record),
416	        ];
417	        if (record.hostName) parts.push(`Host: ${record.hostName}`);
418	        if (record.purpose) parts.push(`Purpose: ${record.purpose}`);
419	        if (record.visitorPhone) parts.push(`Phone: ${record.visitorPhone}`);
420	        return parts.join(" | ");
421	      });
422	
423	      await sendMessage(
424	        msg.chat.id,
425	        `👥 *Today's Visitors*\nSource: live visitor management system\n\n${lines.join("\n")}`,
426	        { parseMode: "Markdown" },
427	      );
428	      break;
429	    }
430	
431	    case "/inventory": {
432	      const agent = mastra.getAgent("queryAgent");
433	      if (!agent) return;
434	      const result = await agent.generate([
435	        { role: "user", content: "Show me today's inventory updates" },
436	      ]);
437	      await sendNonEmptyResponse(
438	        msg.chat.id,
439	        result.text,
440	        "I could not generate the inventory summary right now.",
441	        { parseMode: "Markdown" },
442	      );
443	      break;
444	    }
445	
446	    case "/facilities": {
447	      const agent = mastra.getAgent("queryAgent");
448	      if (!agent) return;
449	      const result = await agent.generate([
450	        { role: "user", content: "Show me open facility requests" },
451	      ]);
452	      await sendNonEmptyResponse(
453	        msg.chat.id,
454	        result.text,
455	        "I could not generate the facility summary right now. Please try again.",
456	        { parseMode: "Markdown" },
457	      );
458	      break;
459	    }
460	
461	    case "/assets": {
462	      const agent = mastra.getAgent("queryAgent");
463	      if (!agent) return;
464	      const result = await agent.generate([
465	        { role: "user", content: "Show me asset tracking status" },
466	      ]);
467	      await sendNonEmptyResponse(
468	        msg.chat.id,
469	        result.text,
470	        "I could not generate the asset summary right now.",
471	        { parseMode: "Markdown" },
472	      );
473	      break;
474	    }
475	
476	    case "/whereami":
477	      await replyWithChatDetails(msg);
478	      break;
479	
480	    case "/cafeteria":
481	    case "/canteen":
482	      await sendCafeteriaMiniAppButton(msg.chat.id);
483	      break;
484	
485	    case "/help":
486	      await sendMessage(
487	        msg.chat.id,
488	        `🤖 *Office Operations Intelligence Bot*
489	
490	*Commands:*
491	/summary — Today's full operations summary
492	/visitors — Today's visitor list
493	/cafeteria — Open cafeteria ordering app
494	/inventory — Inventory status
495	/facilities — Open maintenance requests
496	/assets — Asset tracking status
497	/sopstats — Daily SOP progress summary
498	/whereami — Show this chat ID
499	/export — Sync all data to Google Sheets
500	/reset — Delete DB, Pinecone, and Sheets data
501	/sop — Daily SOP checklist
502	/staff — Staff registry management
503	/help — This message
504	
505	*Visitor Commands:*
506	/invite Name, purpose, host, date, email, start: HH:MM, end: HH:MM — Invite a visitor
507	/guard add "Name" PIN [language] — Create guard account
508	/lockdown — 🚨 Emergency visitor headcount
509	
510	*Staff Commands:*

515	/staff import — Import from data/staff.csv
516	/staff link <id> <channel> <uid> — Link to platform

518	
519	*Natural Language Queries:*

526	
527	Just type your question and I'll find the answer! 🔍`,
528	        { parseMode: "Markdown" },
529	      );
530	      break;
531	
532	    case "/export": {
533	      const bot = getBot();
