535	      await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, "📊 Syncing data to Google Sheets...");
536	      const exportResult = await syncToGoogleSheets();

541	    case "/reset": {

592	// ─── Staff Command Handler ────────────────────────────────
593	
594	async function handleStaffCommand(msg: TelegramBot.Message, args: string[]): Promise<void> {
595	  const subCmd = args[0]?.toLowerCase() || "help";
596	
597	  switch (subCmd) {
598	    case "attendance": {
599	      const staff = await queryStaffDirectory();
600	      const activeStaff = staff.filter((s) => s.attendanceStatus === 'in');
601	      
602	      if (activeStaff.length === 0) {
603	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, "🏢 No staff members are currently marked IN.");
604	        return;
605	      }
606	
607	      const lines = activeStaff.map((s) => {
608	        return `👤 *${s.name}* (${s.role})${s.department ? ` - ${s.department}` : ''}`;
609	      });
610	      
611	      await sendMessage(
612	        msg.chat.id, 
613	        `🏢 *Staff Currently In Office* (${activeStaff.length})\n\n${lines.join('\n')}`, 
614	        { parseMode: "Markdown" }
615	      );
616	      break;
617	    }
618	
619	    case "list": {
620	      const staff = await getAllActiveStaff();
621	      if (staff.length === 0) {
622	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, "📋 No staff members registered yet.\nUse `/staff add \"Name\" role` to add one.", { parseMode: "Markdown" });
623	        return;
624	      }
625	
626	      const lines = staff.map((s, i) => {
627	        const parts = [`${i + 1}. *${s.name}* (${s.role})`];
628	        if (s.phone) parts.push(`📱 ${s.phone}`);
629	        if (s.gender) parts.push(`${s.gender === "male" ? "♂" : s.gender === "female" ? "♀" : "⚧"}`);
630	        if (s.department) parts.push(`🏢 ${s.department}`);
631	        if (s.language) parts.push(`🗣 ${s.language}`);
632	        if (s.channels && s.channels.length > 0) {
633	          const chLinks = s.channels.map((c) => `${c.channel}:${c.channelUid}`).join(", ");
634	          parts.push(`🔗 ${chLinks}`);
635	        }
636	        parts.push(`\`${s.id.slice(0, 8)}\``);
637	        return parts.join(" | ");
638	      });
639	
640	      await sendMessage(
641	        msg.chat.id,
642	        `👥 *Staff Directory* (${staff.length} members)\n\n${lines.join("\n")}`,
643	        { parseMode: "Markdown" },
644	      );
645	      break;
646	    }
647	
648	    case "add": {
649	      // /staff add "Name" role [phone] [gender] [department]
650	      // Parse quoted name
651	      const restText = args.slice(1).join(" ");
652	      const quotedMatch = restText.match(/^"([^"]+)"\s+(.*)$/);
653	      let name: string;
654	      let remaining: string;
655	
656	      if (quotedMatch) {
657	        name = quotedMatch[1]!;
658	        remaining = quotedMatch[2]!;
659	      } else {
660	        // No quotes — first arg is name, rest follows
661	        name = args[1] || "";
662	        remaining = args.slice(2).join(" ");
663	      }
664	
665	      if (!name) {
666	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, '⚠️ Usage: `/staff add "Full Name" role [phone] [gender] [department] [language]`\nRoles: manager, lead, staff\nLanguages: hindi, english, hinglish', { parseMode: "Markdown" });
667	        return;
668	      }
669	
670	      const parts = remaining.split(/\s+/);
671	      const role = parts[0]?.toLowerCase();
672	      if (!role || !["manager", "lead", "staff"].includes(role)) {
673	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `⚠️ Invalid role "${role}". Must be: manager, lead, or staff.`);
674	        return;
675	      }
676	
677	      const phone = parts[1] || undefined;
678	      const gender = parts[2]?.toLowerCase() as "male" | "female" | "other" | undefined;
679	      const department = parts[3] || undefined;
680	      const language = parts[4]?.toLowerCase() || undefined;
681	
682	      try {
683	        const id = await addStaff({
684	          name,
685	          role: role as StaffRole,
686	          phone,
687	          gender: gender && ["male", "female", "other"].includes(gender) ? gender : undefined,
688	          department,
689	          language,
690	        });
691	        await refreshStaffCache();
692	        await sendMessage(
693	          msg.chat.id,
694	          `✅ Staff added: *${name}* (${role})\nID: \`${id.slice(0, 8)}\``,
695	          { parseMode: "Markdown" },
696	        );
697	      } catch (error) {
698	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `❌ Failed to add staff: ${getErrorMessage(error)}`);
699	      }
700	      break;
701	    }
702	
703	    case "update": {
704	      // /staff update <id> <field> <value>
705	      const staffId = args[1];
706	      const field = args[2]?.toLowerCase();
707	      const value = args.slice(3).join(" ");
708	
709	      if (!staffId || !field || !value) {
710	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, "⚠️ Usage: `/staff update <id> <field> <value>`\nFields: name, phone, gender, role, department", { parseMode: "Markdown" });
711	        return;
712	      }
713	
714	      const validFields = ["name", "phone", "gender", "role", "department", "language"];
715	      if (!validFields.includes(field)) {
716	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `⚠️ Invalid field "${field}". Valid: ${validFields.join(", ")}`);
717	        return;
718	      }
719	
720	      try {
721	        // Find staff by ID prefix
722	        const allStaff = await getAllActiveStaff();
723	        const match = allStaff.find((s) => s.id.startsWith(staffId));
724	        if (!match) {
725	          await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `⚠️ No staff found with ID starting with "${staffId}"`);
726	          return;
727	        }
728	
729	        await updateStaff(match.id, { [field]: value } as any);
730	        await refreshStaffCache();
731	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `✅ Updated *${match.name}*: ${field} = "${value}"`, { parseMode: "Markdown" });
732	      } catch (error) {
733	        await sendMessage(msg.chat.id, `❌ Failed: ${getErrorMessage(error)}`);
734	      }
735	      break;

97	export async function resetDatabase(): Promise<{
98	  clearedTables: readonly string[];
99	}> {

111	function createPostgresCompatClient(): Client {
112	  return {
113	    async execute(statement: SqlStatement): Promise<SqlResult> {
114	      const normalized = normalizePostgresStatement(statement);
115	      if (!normalized.sql.trim()) return { rows: [], rowsAffected: 0 };
116	      const result = await getPostgresPool().query(normalized.sql, normalized.args);
117	      return {
118	        rows: result.rows,
119	        rowsAffected: result.rowCount ?? 0,
120	      };
121	    },
122	    async executeMultiple(sql: string): Promise<void> {
123	      for (const statement of splitSqlStatements(sql)) {
124	        const normalized = normalizePostgresStatement(statement);
125	        if (normalized.sql.trim()) {
126	          await getPostgresPool().query(normalized.sql, normalized.args);
127	        }
128	      }
129	    },
130	    async batch(statements: readonly SqlStatement[]): Promise<SqlResult[]> {
131	      const client = await getPostgresPool().connect();
132	      try {
133	        await client.query("BEGIN");
134	        const results: SqlResult[] = [];
135	        for (const statement of statements) {
136	          const normalized = normalizePostgresStatement(statement);
137	          if (!normalized.sql.trim()) {
138	            results.push({ rows: [], rowsAffected: 0 });
139	            continue;
140	          }
141	          const result = await client.query(normalized.sql, normalized.args);
142	          results.push({ rows: result.rows, rowsAffected: result.rowCount ?? 0 });
143	        }
144	        await client.query("COMMIT");
145	        return results;
146	      } catch (error) {
147	        await client.query("ROLLBACK");
148	        throw error;
149	      } finally {
150	        client.release();
151	      }
152	    },
153	  };
154	}
155	
156	function normalizePostgresStatement(statement: SqlStatement): { sql: string; args: SqlArgs } {
157	  const rawSql = typeof statement === "string" ? statement : statement.sql;
158	  const args = typeof statement === "string" ? [] : statement.args ?? [];
159	  let sql = rawSql.trim();
160	
161	  if (!sql) {
162	    return { sql: "", args };
163	  }
164	
165	  sql = sql

  "old_string": "export async function resetDatabase(): Promise<{\n  clearedTables: readonly string[];\n}> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  await db.batch(\n    RESET_TABLES_IN_ORDER.map((table) => `DELETE FROM ${table}`),\n    \"write\",\n  );\n\n  return {\n    clearedTables: RESET_TABLES_IN_ORDER,\n  };\n}",
  "new_string": "export async function resetDatabase(): Promise<{\n  clearedTables: readonly string[];\n}> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  await db.batch(\n    RESET_TABLES_IN_ORDER.map((table) => `DELETE FROM ${table}`),\n    \"write\",\n  );\n\n  return {\n    clearedTables: RESET_TABLES_IN_ORDER,\n  };\n}\n\n// ─── Scoped reset helpers ──────────────────────────────────────\n// Order matters: child tables before parents (FKs). Each helper is\n// idempotent — tables that don't exist are skipped via try/catch in\n// the batch, so first-time installs don't blow up.\n\nconst INVENTORY_RESET_TABLES = [\n  \"inventory_receipts\",\n  \"inventory_mismatch_flags\",\n  \"unresolved_bill_items\",\n  \"inventory_order_items\",\n  \"inventory_orders\",\n  \"inventory_reorder_requests\",\n  \"inventory_issues\",\n  \"inventory_stock\",\n  \"inventory_products\",\n  \"inventory\",\n  \"inventory_name_aliases\",\n  \"product_barcodes\",\n  \"product_aliases\",\n  \"canonical_products\",\n  \"inventory_settings\",\n] as const;\n\nconst VISITOR_RESET_TABLES = [\n  \"visitor_sos_events\",\n  \"visitor_invitation_stakeholders\",\n  \"visitor_audit_log\",\n  \"expected_guest_snapshots\",\n  \"visitor_sessions\",\n  \"offline_sync_events\",\n  \"guard_sessions\",\n  \"guard_push_subscriptions\",\n  \"visitor_broadcasts\",\n  \"visitor_invitations\",\n  \"visitor_locations\",\n  \"visitors\",\n  \"guards\",\n] as const;\n\nconst ALL_DATA_TABLES_EXCEPT_FLOWS_AND_AUTH = [\n  ...INVENTORY_RESET_TABLES,\n  ...VISITOR_RESET_TABLES,\n  \"asset_history\",\n  \"assets\",\n  \"facility_requests\",\n  \"cafeteria_order_items\",\n  \"cafeteria_orders\",\n  \"cafeteria_menu_items\",\n  \"sop_tasks\",\n  \"staff_attendance\",\n  \"staff_channels\",\n  \"staff\",\n  \"raw_messages\",\n  \"sheets_sync_events\",\n  \"audit_log\",\n  \"in_app_notifications\",\n] as const;\n\nconst FLOW_AND_AUTH_TABLES = [\n  \"flow_executions\",\n  \"flow_rules\",\n  \"flow_graphs\",\n  \"password_reset_otps\",\n  \"slack_config\",\n  \"visitor_rules\",\n  \"visitor_templates\",\n  \"role_permissions\",\n  \"user_roles\",\n  \"permissions\",\n  \"roles\",\n  \"users\",\n] as const;\n\nasync function deleteTables(tables: readonly string[]): Promise<{\n  cleared: string[];\n  skipped: { table: string; error: string }[];\n}> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  const cleared: string[] = [];\n  const skipped: { table: string; error: string }[] = [];\n  // Run each delete in its own statement so one missing/bad table\n  // doesn't abort the rest (batch transactions roll the whole thing\n  // back). We're already paying for an expensive operation; per-table\n  // resilience is worth the extra round-trips.\n  for (const table of tables) {\n    try {\n      await db.execute(`DELETE FROM ${table}`);\n      cleared.push(table);\n    } catch (err) {\n      skipped.push({ table, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });\n    }\n  }\n  return { cleared, skipped };\n}\n\n/** Wipe every inventory-related table (orders, catalog, receipts, etc.). */\nexport async function resetInventoryData() {\n  return deleteTables(INVENTORY_RESET_TABLES);\n}\n\n/** Wipe every visitor-related table (visitors, invitations, guards, sessions). */\nexport async function resetVisitorData() {\n  return deleteTables(VISITOR_RESET_TABLES);\n}\n\n/** Wipe all operational data tables. Preserves flows (flow_*), auth\n *  (users/roles/permissions), and the legacy /reset's RESET_TABLES_IN_ORDER\n *  also runs to cover anything we missed above. */\nexport async function resetAllExceptFlowsAndAuth() {\n  const main = await deleteTables(ALL_DATA_TABLES_EXCEPT_FLOWS_AND_AUTH);\n  return main;\n}\n\n/** Wipe EVERYTHING in the office-ops schema — flows, auth, the lot.\n *  Schema (CREATE TABLE statements) is preserved; rows are gone. Flow\n *  definitions live in code and reseed on next startup; users have to\n *  be re-created (super-admin token still works via env). */\nexport async function wipeoutEverything() {\n  const allTables = [...ALL_DATA_TABLES_EXCEPT_FLOWS_AND_AUTH, ...FLOW_AND_AUTH_TABLES];\n  return deleteTables(allTables);\n}"
}

35	export function getPostgresPool(): Pool {
36	  if (pool) return pool;
37	
38	  const connectionString = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
39	  if (!connectionString) {
40	    throw new Error("DATABASE_URL is not configured");
41	  }
42	
43	  // Custom Client that runs `SET search_path` as part of connect, so the
44	  // search_path is in place before pg-pool hands the client out for the
45	  // first query. Using pool.on("connect", ...) is not safe — pg-pool emits
46	  // the event but does not block the next query on the SET completing,
47	  // so concurrent queries on a freshly-spawned connection can race and
48	  // resolve unqualified table names against the wrong search_path (we
49	  // saw `staff_channels` fail to resolve when 130+ queries fired from
50	  // `Promise.all` during staff cache load). Neon's pooler also rejects
51	  // `search_path` as a startup parameter, so we set it via SET at the
52	  // JS layer, chained into the connect callback.
53	  const SEARCH_PATH_SQL = `SET search_path TO ${officeOpsSchemaName()},public`;
54	  class SchemaAwareClient extends PgClient {
55	    override connect(callback?: any): any {
56	      if (typeof callback === "function") {
57	        return super.connect((err: Error | null) => {
58	          if (err) return callback(err);
59	          super.query(SEARCH_PATH_SQL, (setErr: Error | null) => {
60	            callback(setErr);
61	          });
62	        });
63	      }
64	      return (super.connect() as unknown as Promise<unknown>)
65	        .then(() => super.query(SEARCH_PATH_SQL))
66	        .then(() => undefined);
67	    }
68	  }
69	
70	  pool = new Pool({
71	    Client: SchemaAwareClient,
72	    connectionString: normalizePostgresConnectionString(connectionString),
73	    keepAlive: false,
74	    idleTimeoutMillis: 10000,
75	    connectionTimeoutMillis: 5000,
76	  });
77	
78	  // Prevent unhandled 'error' events from crashing the process when Neon
79	  // terminates idle connections — pg-pool emits on the pool, not the caller.
80	  pool.on("error", (err) => {
81	    console.error("[postgres] Idle client error (connection terminated):", err.message);
82	  });
83	
84	  return pool;
85	}

> AGENT

Clean. Restart `office-ops-engine`.

**Why this happened** — Neon's pooler closes idle Postgres connections aggressively (a few seconds to a minute, depending on tier). Our pool was running with `keepAlive: false`, so the OS sent no TCP keepalive packets and the socket silently died. Next batch tick the pool handed out the stale client → "Connection terminated due to connection timeout." The catch in the batch processor swallows it and we retry, but the log line is loud.

**What changed** — pool config:
- `keepAlive: true` + `keepAliveInitialDelayMillis: 10_000` — the OS starts pinging Neon after 10s of socket idle, so Neon never sees the connection as idle. This is the main fix.
- `connectionTimeoutMillis: 10_000` (was 5s) — cold Neon takes a few seconds to wake; 5s was tight.
- `idleTimeoutMillis: 30_000` (was 10s) — keep connections warm a bit longer instead of churning them every cycle.
- `max: 10` — explicit cap (pg-pool default is 10 too, but stated for clarity).
- The pool's `error` event handler is now `console.warn`, not `console.error`, since it's expected behaviour — a connection in the idle list got reaped before we could use it; the pool just opens a new one. No action needed.

You may still see one or two of these on first start before keepalive kicks in. After a few minutes of warm traffic they should disappear.

> AGENT

Two separate problems in that log — let me explain both and fix the one that's a real bug.

**1. 401 storm on `/api/inventory/canonical-products`** (~30 requests in 10 seconds)

This isn't a server bug — it's your **admin session token expired** (or the Bearer header was lost). Every dashboard query that depends on the catalog fires immediately, gets 401, and on 401 the dashboard's auth check trips. With React Query default refetch-on-focus + multiple components reading the same query, it cascades.

The fast cadence (4–6 requests/sec) tells me the dashboard is in a re-render loop: when `useQuery` returns an error, some upstream `useEffect` flips state, the component re-mounts, the query re-fires. The cure is to **re-login** (click your avatar → log out → log in). If it happens immediately again after login, the token TTL is short or the cookie/local-storage write is failing.

If you want, I can add a guard in the dashboard so that on 401 we stop retrying and redirect to the login screen instead of grinding — but the quick fix right now is a logout + login.

**2. Sheets `429 Too Many Requests`** — **real bug, fixable now.**

Every receipt and every product write was triggering a full Catalog-tab rebuild (which is a sheet `get` + `clear` + `update` = 3 API reads/writes minimum). Over a short burst of receipts/registrations, we blew the per-minute quota. Debounce the catalog sync — coalesce many triggers within 15s into one push.

  "new_string": "/**\n * Push the canonical catalog to the linked Google Sheet, NOW.\n * Most callers should use `syncCatalogTabToSheet` instead, which\n * debounces bursts of triggers (every bill validate, every product\n * create, every field registration) into a single push and so avoids\n * the Sheets `Read requests per minute per user` quota.\n */\nasync function syncCatalogTabToSheetNow(siteId: string): Promise<void> {\n  const [spreadsheetId, ownerEmail] = await Promise.all([\n    getSetting(siteId, SHEET_ID_KEY),\n    getSetting(siteId, SHEET_OWNER_KEY),\n  ]);\n  if (!spreadsheetId || !ownerEmail) return;\n  const sheets = await getAdminSheetsClient(ownerEmail);\n  if (!sheets) return;\n  const rows = await listCatalogForSheet(siteId);\n  const sheetRows = rows.map((r) => [\n    r.canonical_name,\n    r.category ?? \"\",\n    r.unit,\n    String(r.pack_size),\n    r.last_price != null ? Burst\n// of 30 validations → one Sheets write, not thirty. Critical to staying\n// under Sheets' 60 reads/min/user quota.\nconst CATALOG_SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS = 15_000;\nconst pendingCatalogSync = new Map<string, ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>();\n\nfunction syncCatalogTabToSheet(siteId: string): Promise<void> {\n  const existing = pendingCatalogSync.get(siteId);\n  if (existing) clearTimeout(existing);\n  const handle = setTimeout(() => {\n    pendingCatalogSync.delete(siteId);\n    void syncCatalogTabToSheetNow(siteId).catch((err) => {\n      logError(\"[Inventory] debounced catalog sync failed\", err, {\n        scope: \"inventory.sheets\",\n      });\n    });\n  }, CATALOG_SYNC_DEBOUNCE_MS);\n  pendingCatalogSync.set(siteId, handle);\n  return Promise.resolve();\n}"
}

> AGENT

Clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`.**

**Recap:**

**Problem A — 401 storm on `/api/inventory/canonical-products`** (the bursty repeat requests). That's the **dashboard side, not the server**. Your admin Bearer token is invalid (expired or never set). Every dashboard query that hits `/api/inventory/*` returns 401 immediately. React Query, combined with whatever component subscribes to that query, retries on each render. **Log out and log back in** — the next reload will use a fresh token and the storm stops. If you want, I can add a 401 interceptor that triggers a logout-and-redirect once instead of letting it grind; tell me and I'll wire it.

**Problem B — Sheets 429** (`Quota exceeded for Read requests per minute per user`). Real backend bug, now fixed.

Each receipt / product create / field registration was triggering an immediate Catalog rebuild (3+ Sheets API calls each). A short burst blew Google's 60-reads/min/user quota. Now:

- `syncCatalogTabToSheet(siteId)` is a **debounced trampoline**: 15-second window. Thirty triggers in five seconds → one Sheets push, not thirty.
- The explicit admin endpoint `POST /api/inventory/sheet/sync-catalog` now calls `syncCatalogTabToSheetNow(...)` directly (immediate; admin asked for it).
- The Received tab append-per-receipt is one row per write, can't safely be coalesced (would lose per-row history), so it stays as-is — that path is well under the quota.

If the quota error returns despite this, we can lengthen the debounce window or batch Received-tab writes too.

Inferred from the\n   *  item name when not a separate column. */\n  unit_type: string | null;\n  /** Numeric value of one pack (\"750\" for \"750G\", \"1\" for \"1L\").\n   *  Null when we can't tell. */\n  unit_value: number | null;\n  /** High-level category — Grocery / Cleaning / Snacks / Beverages /\n   *  Dairy / Office / etc. Inferred from the item name. */\n  category: string | null;\n  /** Per-unit rate from the bill (\"RATE\"). */\n  rate: number | null;\n  /** Line total (\"VALUE\"). */\n  value: number | null;\n  /** HSN if present on the bill; nice-to-have, never required. */\n  hsn_code: string | null;\n};\n\nexport type ExtractedBill = {\n  vendor_name: string | null;\n  bill_number: string | null;\n  bill_date: string | null;\n  line_items: BillLineItem[];\n  grand_total: number | null;\n};\n\nconst EXTRACTION_PROMPT = `You are a bill/receipt data extractor for an Indian office operations system.\n\nVendor bill layouts vary widely. Different vendors put the columns in different\norders, and some omit columns entirely (HSN, tax category, etc. may be missing).\nYour job is to extract the USEFUL fields for each line item — not just transcribe\nthe columns you see. Pull values from anywhere on the line (column, item-name\nsuffix like \"750G\", row totals, etc.).\n\nFor each line item, return these fields (some inferred from the item name when\nnot a separate column):\n\n  - item_purchased  — exact item text as written on the bill\n  - qty             — how many packs/units arrived (number)\n  - unit_type       — \"kg\" | \"g\" | \"l\" | \"ml\" | \"pcs\" | \"pack\" | \"box\"\n                      (lowercase; pick the best fit; null only if you really\n                      cannot tell)\n  - unit_value      — numeric size of one pack: 750 for \"750G\", 1 for \"1L\",\n                      1 for an unspecified piece; null if uncertain\n  - category        — a short high-level grocery category like\n                      \"Grocery\" | \"Snacks\" | \"Beverages\" | \"Dairy\" |\n                      \"Cleaning\" | \"Bakery\" | \"Personal Care\" | \"Office\" |\n                      \"Stationery\". Infer from item name. Null only if you\n                      truly cannot guess.\n  - rate            — per-unit price from the bill (number, no currency)\n  - value           — line total (number, no currency)\n  - hsn_code        — only if the bill has an HSN column; null otherwise\n\nExamples (different vendor layouts):\n\n  Dmart row:  \"1. 19041090  2  KELLOGS MUESLI FRUIT N NUT 750G  3.0  349.0  1047.0\"\n  →\n    { item_purchased: \"KELLOGS MUESLI FRUIT N NUT 750G\",\n      qty: 3, unit_type: \"g\", unit_value: 750, category: \"Breakfast\",\n      rate: 349, value: 1047, hsn_code: \"19041090\" }\n\n  Kirana row: \"Wagh Bakri 1kg bks1   5   340.00   1700.00\"\n  →\n    { item_purchased: \"Wagh Bakri 1kg bks1\",\n      qty: 5, unit_type: \"kg\", unit_value: 1, category: \"Beverages\",\n      rate: 340, value: 1700, hsn_code: null }\n\n  Cleaning shop row: \"Vim dishwash 500ml   12   45   540\"\n  →\n    { item_purchased: \"Vim dishwash 500ml\",\n      qty: 12, unit_type: \"ml\", unit_value: 500, category: \"Cleaning\",\n      rate: 45, value: 540, hsn_code: null }\n\nAlso return bill metadata, but DO NOT invent values when they're missing.\nIf the bill has no vendor name / bill number / date visible, return null —\nthe admin will fill them in:\n\n  - vendor_name\n  - bill_number\n  - bill_date         (YYYY-MM-DD if you can convert; null otherwise)\n  - grand_total       (number, no currency)\n\nOutput strict JSON in this exact shape — no markdown fences, no commentary:\n\n{\n  \"vendor_name\": \"string or null\",\n  \"bill_number\": \"string or null\",\n  \"bill_date\":   \"YYYY-MM-DD or null\",\n  \"grand_total\": 3840.0,\n  \"line_items\": [\n    { \"sr_no\": 1, \"item_purchased\": \"…\", \"qty\": 3,\n      \"unit_type\": \"g\", \"unit_value\": 750, \"category\": \"Breakfast\",\n      \"rate\": 349.0, \"value\": 1047.0, \"hsn_code\": \"19041090\" }\n  ]\n}\n\nRules:\n  - Extract EVERY line item, even if partially legible.\n  - Preserve the EXACT item name as written (do not correct spelling).\n  - qty / rate / value / unit_value must be numbers, not strings.\n  - For categories you're not 100% sure about, pick the closest sensible\n    bucket — don't return null just because the bill doesn't say so.\n  - If the bill is in Hindi or another script, keep item names in that script.`;"

We\n  // never auto-apply a suggestion because the alias cache can carry\n  // bad mappings from prior test runs, and silently overwriting the\n  // extracted name has burned us.\n  return {\n    tempId: it.tempId,\n    bill_item_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    canonical_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    category: \"\",\n    hsn_code: it.hsn_code ?? \"\",\n    qty: it.qty,\n    rate: it.rate,\n    value: it.value,\n    unit:\n      it.unit_hint && UNIT_OPTIONS.includes(it.unit_hint) ? it.unit_hint : \"pcs\",\n    pack_size: 1,\n    action: \"create_new\",\n    product_id: null,\n    suggestions: it.suggestions,\n  };\n}",
  "new_string": "function itemToRow(it: BillExtractItem): ReviewRow {\n  // Pre-fill what the LLM extracted. Admin can edit anything; we never\n  // auto-apply a catalog suggestion because the alias cache has burned\n  // us before — admin clicks a suggestion explicitly to map.\n  const rawUnit = (it.unit_type ?? \"\").toLowerCase();\n  return {\n    tempId: it.tempId,\n    bill_item_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    canonical_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    category: it.category ?? \"\",\n    hsn_code: it.hsn_code ?? \"\",\n    qty: it.qty,\n    rate: it.rate,\n    value: it.value,\n    unit: UNIT_OPTIONS.includes(rawUnit) ? rawUnit : (rawUnit || \"pcs\"),\n    pack_size: it.unit_value && it.unit_value > 0 ? it.unit_value : 1,\n    action: \"create_new\",\n    product_id: null,\n    suggestions: it.suggestions,\n  };\n}"
}

> AGENT

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`** so the new extraction prompt is used; hard-reload the dashboard.

**What changed:**

**Backend extractor (`bill-extractor.ts`)**
- LLM is now asked for **name, qty, unit_type, unit_value, category, rate, value** explicitly, with worked examples for Dmart-style, Kirana-style, and cleaning-shop-style rows. The prompt is layout-agnostic — extract the useful values from wherever they appear on the line, not just from named columns.
- **HSN demoted to bonus-if-present.** No longer required; null when absent.
- **Category, unit_type, unit_value, rate, value, qty** are the high-confidence required-or-best-effort fields. Category is inferred from item name even when not on the bill.
- `vendor_name`, `bill_number`, `bill_date`, `grand_total` are still extracted but **explicitly allowed to be null** — the prompt tells the model not to invent them.
- Parser normalises everything: numeric coercion that returns null on bad input, string trim with empty→null, fallback to old field names (`unit`, `pack_size`) for backwards compat with any cached state.
- Removed unused `tax_total` from the response.

**Dashboard bill review**
- `itemToRow` pre-fills the review row from the LLM's `category`, `unit_type`, `unit_value` (and falls back to sensible defaults when null). So Dmart's `KELLOGS MUESLI FRUIT N NUT 750G` arrives with `unit=g, pack_size=750, category=Breakfast/Grocery` already filled in. Admin edits anything they want.
- **Bill metadata (Vendor / Bill # / Date) is empty-allowed.** When the LLM couldn't find a value, the field's label shows `VENDOR · missing` in amber, the input gets an amber border + light yellow background, and a placeholder like `Add vendor…`. Admin can leave the bill blank and validate (no hard requirement) or fill in.
- HSN field is still there but you can leave it blank — the validate path treats it as optional. No more pressure.

Test with the Dmart row from your example: the LLM should now return `item_purchased: "KELLOGS MUESLI FRUIT N NUT 750G"`, `qty: 3`, `unit_type: "g"`, `unit_value: 750`, `category: "Breakfast"` (or similar), `rate: 349`, `value: 1047`, `hsn_code: "19041090"`. The review row will arrive with all of those pre-filled — admin just confirms or maps to an existing standard product.

Admin can edit anything; we never\n  // auto-apply a catalog suggestion because the alias cache has burned\n  // us before — admin clicks a suggestion explicitly to map.\n  const rawUnit = (it.unit_type ?? \"\").toLowerCase();\n  return {\n    tempId: it.tempId,\n    bill_item_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    canonical_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    category: it.category ?? \"\",\n    hsn_code: it.hsn_code ?? \"\",\n    qty: it.qty,\n    rate: it.rate,\n    value: it.value,\n    unit: UNIT_OPTIONS.includes(rawUnit) ? rawUnit : (rawUnit || \"pcs\"),\n    pack_size: it.unit_value && it.unit_value > 0 ? it.unit_value : 1,\n    action: \"create_new\",\n    product_id: null,\n    suggestions: it.suggestions,\n  };\n}",
  "new_string": "function itemToRow(it: BillExtractItem): ReviewRow {\n  const rawUnit = (it.unit_type ?? \"\").toLowerCase();\n\n  // Exact-name match in the catalog (case-insensitive). The backend's\n  // suggester returns this with method=\"exact\" + score=1. When we see\n  // it, auto-apply — the alias cache poisoning that bit us before is\n  // only a risk for fuzzy / alias / normalized matches, NOT exact-name\n  // hits, which are deterministic.\n  const exact = it.suggestions.find(\n    (s) =>\n      s.method === \"exact\" ||\n      s.canonicalName.trim().toLowerCase() === it.bill_item_name.trim().toLowerCase(),\n  );\n\n  if (exact) {\n    return {\n      tempId: it.tempId,\n      bill_item_name: it.bill_item_name,\n      canonical_name: exact.canonicalName,\n      category: exact.category ?? it.category ?? \"\",\n      hsn_code: exact.hsnCode ?? it.hsn_code ?? \"\",\n      qty: it.qty,\n      rate: it.rate,\n      value: it.value,\n      unit: exact.unit,\n      pack_size: exact.packSize,\n      action: \"use_existing\",\n      product_id: exact.productId,\n      suggestions: it.suggestions,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // No exact hit — pre-fill from the LLM's extraction and let the admin\n  // pick a suggestion (or type into the combobox) if they want to map.\n  return {\n    tempId: it.tempId,\n    bill_item_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    canonical_name: it.bill_item_name,\n    category: it.category ?? \"\",\n    hsn_code: it.hsn_code ?? \"\",\n    qty: it.qty,\n    rate: it.rate,\n    value: it.value,\n    unit: UNIT_OPTIONS.includes(rawUnit) ? rawUnit : (rawUnit || \"pcs\"),\n    pack_size: it.unit_value && it.unit_value > 0 ? it.unit_value : 1,\n    action: \"create_new\",\n    product_id: null,\n    suggestions: it.suggestions,\n  };\n}"

> AGENT

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`**; hard-reload the dashboard.

**What changed:**

1. **Manual order creation (Orders tab).** New "**+ New order**" button in the Orders tab header. Clicking it shows an inline form (Vendor / Bill # / Bill date — all optional, with the same `FieldLabel` style as the rest of the tab) and a Create button. On save, a server-side empty order is created via the new `POST /api/inventory/orders` endpoint; the new card appears at the top of the list. Admin then expands it and uses the existing "**+ Add an item from catalog…**" row to add line items one by one. So even if extraction is broken or the vendor never gives a bill, the system stays usable end-to-end.

2. **Bill upload state survives tab switches.** `BillUploadTab` is now always mounted; the parent toggles `display: block/none` instead of conditionally rendering. So your extracted line items, edits, file preview, and billMeta inputs stay alive when you peek at Orders/Catalog/Export and come back. The state is wiped only when you explicitly click **Discard** or **Validate & save** — exactly like you asked.

3. **Exact-name match now auto-applies.** `itemToRow` checks the suggester's response for an entry with `method === "exact"` (or a case-insensitive byte-equal canonical name). When found, the row arrives **pre-mapped to the standard product** — name, category, unit, pack size, HSN are copied from the catalog entry, `action = use_existing`, `product_id` set. The pill at the top right now reads **"✓ Matched to standard"** (green). Your `Vim Dishwash Liquid Gel Lemon 2Ltr` bill row will now arrive already mapped to the same-named catalog entry instead of registering as a duplicate. Lower-confidence hits (alias, HSN-fuzzy, normalized) still surface as the "Did you mean: …" pill so the admin clicks to accept — that's the path that historically had bad-alias poisoning, so we keep it manual.

If you ever want exact-match auto-apply to also fire on suggestion `score === 1.0` from `alias` (admin-validated aliases that we trust completely), tell me and I'll widen the auto-apply rule. For now it's deliberately the strictest possible: byte-equal canonical name.

> AGENT

No. The dashboard deliberately does not use Redux/Zustand/Jotai/etc. The stack is:

- **TanStack Query** (`@tanstack/react-query`) for all **server state** — every `/api/*` call (orders, catalog, sheet info, compliance, etc.) goes through `useQuery` / `useMutation`. Cache, refetch, invalidation, and optimistic updates are all handled there.
- **React's built-in `useState`/`useReducer`** for **local UI state** (form drafts, which tab is open, modal visibility, the bill-upload review rows, the sheet-attach input, etc.).
- **TanStack Router** for URL/route state.

The CLAUDE.md for this subrepo is explicit about it: *"Don't introduce Redux / Zustand / Context for server data — Query already handles cache, refetch, mutation."*

This is intentional and works well here for two reasons:

1. **Most "state" in this app is server state.** Orders, catalog, receipts, sheet info — all of it lives on the backend. React Query owns it. There's no client-side derived data to manage globally.
2. **Local UI state is local.** Each form/modal owns its inputs and discards them on close — no need for a global store.

The one piece of state that's slightly awkward — the bill upload form being wiped on tab switch — was solved one turn ago by keeping `BillUploadTab` mounted (`display: none` when inactive) rather than reaching for a state manager. That's the right scope for the problem.

If we ever needed cross-route persistent UI state (e.g. "you were halfway through an order draft and clicked away to another section"), the right step would be a small Zustand or context store for *that specific need* — not a global rewrite. For the inventory section as it stands, no state library is needed.

  "new_string": "  /** A scanned code is only a usable product barcode if it looks like\n   *  one — UPC/EAN/ITF/Code128 are alphanumeric (mostly digits) with\n   *  no whitespace. QR codes / data matrix often carry URLs and free\n   *  text; routing those into the barcode field caused the bug where\n   *  a URL like https://… ended up in the Receiving form's barcode\n   *  slot. Reject anything that fails this filter. */\n  const looksLikeBarcode = (raw: string): boolean => {\n    const v = raw.trim();\n    if (v.length < 4 || v.length > 32) return false;\n    if (/^https?:\\/\\//i.test(v)) return false;\n    if (/\\s/.test(v)) return false;\n    // Allow alphanumerics, dashes, underscores (covers EAN/UPC + serials).\n    return /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(v);\n  };\n\n  /** Entry point for both camera scans (after the 2-read gate) and manual entry. */\n  const acceptCode = useCallback(\n    (raw: string) => {\n      if (acceptedRef.current) return;\n      if (!looksLikeBarcode(raw)) {\n        // Soft-reject: brief haptic so the user knows the read fired,\n        // but don't navigate. The camera will detect again on the next\n        // frame, hopefully landing on the actual product barcode.\n        haptic.warn();\n        return;\n      }\n      acceptedRef.current = true;\n      haptic.success();\n      flash();\n      routeFor(raw.trim());\n    },\n    [flash, routeFor],\n  );"
}

  "old_string": "export async function syncStockFromRemote(row: {\n  barcode: string;\n  name: string;\n  category: string | null;\n  unit: string | null;\n  on_hand: number;\n  threshold: number;\n}): Promise<void> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  await db.runAsync(\n    `INSERT INTO stock_levels (barcode, name, category, unit, on_hand, threshold, updated_at)\n     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\n     ON CONFLICT(barcode) DO UPDATE SET\n       name=excluded.name,\n       category=excluded.category,\n       unit=excluded.unit,\n       on_hand=excluded.on_hand,\n       threshold=excluded.threshold,\n       updated_at=excluded.updated_at`,\n    [row.barcode, row.name, row.category, row.unit, row.on_hand, row.threshold, now()]\n  );\n}",
  "new_string": "export async function syncStockFromRemote(row: {\n  barcode: string;\n  name: string;\n  category: string | null;\n  unit: string | null;\n  on_hand: number;\n  threshold: number;\n}): Promise<void> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  await db.runAsync(\n    `INSERT INTO stock_levels (barcode, name, category, unit, on_hand, threshold, updated_at)\n     VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\n     ON CONFLICT(barcode) DO UPDATE SET\n       name=excluded.name,\n       category=excluded.category,\n       unit=excluded.unit,\n       on_hand=excluded.on_hand,\n       threshold=excluded.threshold,\n       updated_at=excluded.updated_at`,\n    [row.barcode, row.name, row.category, row.unit, row.on_hand, row.threshold, now()]\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Replace the local stock cache with whatever the remote returned.\n * Upsert every remote row, then drop locally-cached rows the remote\n * no longer knows about. Prevents stale items lingering after an admin\n * wipes inventory data on the server.\n */\nexport async function replaceStockFromRemote(\n  rows: Array<{\n    barcode: string;\n    name: string;\n    category: string | null;\n    unit: string | null;\n    on_hand: number;\n    threshold: number;\n  }>,\n): Promise<void> {\n  const db = await getDb();\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    await syncStockFromRemote(row);\n  }\n  if (rows.length === 0) {\n    // Remote is empty — wipe local too.\n    await db.runAsync(`DELETE FROM stock_levels`);\n    return;\n  }\n  const ids = rows.map((r) => `'${String(r.barcode).replace(/'/g, \"''\")}'`).join(',');\n  await db.runAsync(`DELETE FROM stock_levels WHERE barcode NOT IN (${ids})`);\n}"
}

6	/**

14	 * What we DO clear: stock_levels, orders, order_items — pure read
15	 * caches that are re-mirrored from remote on screen focus.

17	 * What we DO NOT clear:

19	 *     Scanner before a remote lookup).
20	 *   - outbox: pending writes destined for the backend.
21	 *   - receipts: local record of what was scanned at the gate.
22	 *
23	 * Gated by an AsyncStorage flag so this only runs once per install.
24	 * Bump the flag suffix if a future reset is needed.
25	 */
26	export async function resetLocalCacheOnce(): Promise<void> {
27	  const done = await AsyncStorage.getItem(FLAG);
28	  if (done) return;
29	  const db = await getDb();
30	  await db.execAsync(`
31	    DELETE FROM stock_levels;
32	    DELETE FROM order_items;
33	    DELETE FROM orders;
34	  `);
35	  await AsyncStorage.setItem(FLAG, '1');

> AGENT

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`**; hard-reload the dashboard; reload Metro for the field-app.

**What's now in place:**

**#1 — Barcode learning updates the Catalog sheet.**
- `POST /api/inventory/canonical-products/learn-barcode` (the guard's explicit learn) and the receipt route's defense-in-depth `learnBarcode` call both now trigger a Catalog-tab refresh.
- Both go through the existing 15-second debouncer, so a burst of scans coalesces into one push and stays under the Sheets quota.
- The Catalog tab's **Barcode** column will fill in as scans happen.

**#2 — "Sync range to sheet" button removed.**
- Every receipt is already auto-appended to the Received tab. The button was triggering a backfill of the same date range, producing exact duplicates.
- The SheetConfigCard now has just **Open sheet ↗** and **Detach** (and the description text). The endpoint `POST /api/inventory/sheet/sync` is still alive on the server in case a manual backfill is ever needed, but no UI surface fires it.

**#3 — URL-in-barcode bug.**
- `ScannerScreen.acceptCode` now soft-rejects anything that doesn't look like a product barcode: must be 4–32 chars, no whitespace, no `http://`/`https://` prefix, and only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. QR codes carrying URLs no longer end up in the Receiving form's barcode slot.
- Rejected reads give a `haptic.warn()` so the guard knows the camera fired; the scanner keeps looking until a real barcode shows up.

**#4 — Stale field-app cache after server wipe.**
- `replaceStockFromRemote(rows)` now exists in `db/stock.ts`: upserts every remote row, then deletes locally-cached rows the remote no longer has. Empty remote = local wiped.
- `StockScreen` and `AlertsScreen` now use it. Alerts also fetches the full stock list (not just the low-or-out subset) so wiped items disappear from alerts too.
- **Settings → Data → "Clear local data"** does an immediate full reset of `stock_levels`, `orders`, `order_items`, `canonical_products`, `product_barcodes`, `products`, and `outbox`, then re-pulls canonical products + orders from the server so the next screen isn't blank. Receipts already scanned and the session token are kept; the guard stays signed in.

If you want the field-app to also fire a "Clear local data" automatically when it notices the server returned drastically smaller counts (e.g. after a wipe), I can add a sentinel check — but the manual button + the replace-not-just-upsert sync should cover the cases you described.

**#1 — bill_date round-trip is broken.** Postgres `DATE` columns come back through the pg driver as JS `Date` objects, which JSON-serialise to `"2026-06-03T00:00:00.000Z"`. HTML `<input type="date">` only accepts bare `YYYY-MM-DD`, so it silently rejects the value and shows the empty placeholder — the date *is* in the DB, the UI just can't render it back.

Three-part defense:

> AGENT

All clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`**, hard-reload the dashboard.

**What's done:**

**Bill date persisted correctly.**
- `listOrdersWithItems` now selects `to_char(bill_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS bill_date`. The pg driver no longer turns the value into a JS `Date` → ISO timestamp, so `<input type="date">` accepts the round-tripped value and the date stays visible after refresh.

**Status column in Export tab now means something useful.**
- Old logic compared `this single receipt's qty` to `total expected qty` — meaningless for partial deliveries (every row showed MISMATCH).
- New logic reads `r.flagged` — i.e. did the guard explicitly raise a mismatch flag at the gate (wrong qty / damaged pack / bad expiry). Values are **`OK`** or **`Flagged`**.
- Column header now has a `title` tooltip explaining what it means (hover over "Status" on the Export table).
- Sheet's Received tab gets the same value pushed through.

**Bill extract no longer 500s on a transient catalog lookup error.**
- Per-line `suggestForBillLine(...)` is now wrapped in try/catch. The whole bill extraction succeeds; rows with a failed suggester come through with `suggestions: []`, and the admin maps them manually. No more "the OCR ran for 60s and then failed completely".
- The actual error is logged with the line item name so we can diagnose if it keeps happening.
- Root-cause defense in the pg pool: every newly-acquired connection now re-runs `SET search_path TO <officeOps>,public` via `pool.on("connect", …)`. The `SchemaAwareClient.connect()` was supposed to do this once, but we'd seen "relation does not exist" after long-running operations (the 60s OCR wait), which is the classic Neon-recycled-the-client scenario. Re-running SET on every acquire is ~1ms and guarantees the path is set.

If the bill-extract failure recurs after this restart, run `bun run scripts/check-sites.ts` once and paste the row — I want to rule out the table actually being absent (which would mean the migration didn't run on this DB).

> AGENT

Found it. **The scanner is configured to read QR codes** (line 48 of `ScannerScreen.tsx`). The Expo dev-client splash screen shows a QR code containing exactly that `exp+field-app://…` URL — when the camera is pointed anywhere near the dev tools, it reads it and dutifully treats it as a barcode. The "fallback" you suspected isn't a code path; it's vision-camera doing what we told it to do.

Fix: drop the 2D codes (QR, data-matrix, PDF-417, Aztec) from the scanner. Product barcodes are always 1D. And tighten the content filter to reject *any* URI scheme.

  "new_string": "  /** A scanned code is only a usable product barcode if it looks like\n   *  one — UPC/EAN/ITF/Code128 are alphanumeric (mostly digits) with\n   *  no whitespace. We already restrict the scanner to 1D code types,\n   *  but defense in depth: also reject any URI-scheme string\n   *  (http://, exp+field-app://, mailto:, tel:, etc.) in case a 1D\n   *  barcode ever carried URL-like text. */\n  const looksLikeBarcode = (raw: string): boolean => {\n    const v = raw.trim();\n    if (v.length < 4 || v.length > 32) return false;\n    // Any URI scheme — \"scheme:\" or \"scheme://\" — is not a product barcode.\n    if (/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i.test(v)) return false;\n    if (/\\s/.test(v)) return false;\n    // Allow alphanumerics, dashes, underscores (covers EAN/UPC + serials).\n    return /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(v);\n  };"
}

> AGENT

Clean. Reload Metro.

**Summary of what was actually happening:**
- The scanner was configured to read 13 code symbologies including `qr`, `data-matrix`, `pdf-417`, and `aztec`. When you ran `npx expo start`, the Expo dev tools displayed a QR code containing exactly that `exp+field-app://expo-development-client/?url=…` URL. The camera saw it and routed the URL through `routeFor()` as if it were a barcode — no fallback code path, just a misconfigured `CODE_TYPES` list.

**Fixes:**
1. **Scanner now only reads 1D product barcodes** (`code-128 / code-39 / code-93 / codabar / ean-13 / ean-8 / itf / upc-a / upc-e`). QR / data-matrix / PDF-417 / Aztec are gone. Physical product labels never use these anyway.
2. **URI-scheme content filter generalised** — used to reject only `http://` / `https://`. Now any `scheme:` prefix (`exp+field-app:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, anything matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:`) is rejected. Defense in depth in case any 1D barcode ever encodes URL-like text.
3. **Manual-entry input now runs the same filter** — paste-from-clipboard / autofill won't sneak URLs in through that path either.

After reloading the field-app, even pointing the camera straight at the Expo dev-client QR won't trigger a scan.

| `Received append skipped (owner Google token missing): owner=…` | The admin who attached the sheet has no Google OAuth refresh token in the `users` table — they signed out of Google or never connected. | That admin re-attaches the sheet (the new OAuth grant saves a fresh refresh token). |
| `Received append skipped (compliance row not found): site=…, receipt=…` | The receipt row wasn't visible to the next SQL — usually site_id mismatch between insert and lookup. | Paste me the receipt id + the field-app's `config.siteId` (Settings → top of screen subtitle, or env). |
| `Received append → "<product>" qty=<n> (receipt=…)` followed by an error stack from `[Inventory] Sheet append failed` | The append is firing but the Sheets API rejects it. Most likely permission or quota. | Paste me the error message. |

184	async function deleteTables(tables: readonly string[]): Promise<{
185	  cleared: string[];
186	  skipped: { table: string; error: string }[];
187	}> {
188	  const db = await getDb();
189	  const cleared: string[] = [];
190	  const skipped: { table: string; error: string }[] = [];
191	  // Run each delete in its own statement so one missing/bad table
192	  // doesn't abort the rest (batch transactions roll the whole thing
193	  // back). We're already paying for an expensive operation; per-table
194	  // resilience is worth the extra round-trips.
195	  for (const table of tables) {
196	    try {
197	      await db.execute(`DELETE FROM ${table}`);
198	      cleared.push(table);
199	    } catch (err) {
200	      skipped.push({ table, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
201	    }
202	  }
203	  return { cleared, skipped };
204	}
205

207	export async function resetInventoryData() {
208	  return deleteTables(INVENTORY_RESET_TABLES);
209	}

212	export async function resetVisitorData() {
213	  return deleteTables(VISITOR_RESET_TABLES);
214	}

216	/** Wipe all operational data tables. Preserves flows (flow_*), auth
217	 *  (users/roles/permissions), and the legacy /reset's RESET_TABLES_IN_ORDER
218	 *  also runs to cover anything we missed above. */

278	function normalizePostgresStatement(statement: SqlStatement): { sql: string; args: SqlArgs } {
279	  const rawSql = typeof statement === "string" ? statement : statement.sql;
280	  const args = typeof statement === "string" ? [] : statement.args ?? [];
281	  let sql = rawSql.trim();
282	
283	  if (!sql) {
284	    return { sql: "", args };
285	  }
286	
287	  sql = sql
288	    .replace(/INSERT\s+OR\s+REPLACE\s+INTO\s+staff_channels\s*\(([^)]+)\)\s*VALUES\s*\(([^)]+)\)/i,
289	      "INSERT INTO staff_channels ($1) VALUES ($2) ON CONFLICT (channel, channel_uid) DO UPDATE SET staff_id = EXCLUDED.staff_id, channel_uname = EXCLUDED.channel_uname, created_at = EXCLUDED.created_at")
290	    .replace(/datetime\(vs\.checkin_time,\s*'\+'\s*\|\|\s*\?\s*\|\|\s*'\s*minutes'\)\s*<\s*\?/gi,
291	      "(vs.checkin_time::timestamptz + (?::int * interval '1 minute')) < ?::timestamptz")
292	    .replace(/datetime\(created_at,\s*'\+'\s*\|\|\s*\?\s*\|\|\s*'\s*hours'\)\s*<\s*datetime\(\?\)/gi,
293	      "(created_at::timestamptz + (?::int * interval '1 hour')) < ?::timestamptz")
294	    .replace(/datetime\(created_at,\s*'\+24 hours'\)\s*<\s*datetime\(\?\)/gi,
295	      "(created_at::timestamptz + interval '24 hours') < ?::timestamptz");
296	
297	  return {
298	    sql: replaceQuestionPlaceholders(sql),
299	    args,
300	  };
301	}
302	
303	function replaceQuestionPlaceholders(sql: string): string {
304	  let index = 0;
305	  let output = "";
306	  let inSingleQuote = false;
307	  for (let i = 0; i < sql.length; i++) {
308	    const char = sql[i];
309	    const next = sql[i + 1];
310	    if (char === "'" && next === "'") {
311	      output += char + next;
312	      i++;
313	      continue;
314	    }
315	    if (char === "'") {
316	      inSingleQuote = !inSingleQuote;
317	      output += char;
318	      continue;
319	    }
320	    if (char === "?" && !inSingleQuote) {
321	      index++;
322	      output += `$${index}`;
323	      continue;
324	    }
325	    output += char;
326	  }
327	  return output;
328	}
329	
330	function splitSqlStatements(sql: string): string[] {
331	  return sql
332	    .split(";")
333	    .map((statement) => statement.trim())
334	    .filter(Boolean);
335	}

> AGENT

Clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`.**

**Root cause:** `key` is a SQL reserved word in some contexts. The query `WHERE site_id = ? AND key = ?` made Postgres' parser choke on the bareword `key`, which manifested as "syntax error at or near AND" (the parser had already accepted `site_id = $1` and then saw `AND key = $2` as malformed). Now every `inventory_settings.key` reference is double-quoted as `"key"`.

You might wonder why Catalog sync seemed to work but Received didn't — both call `getSetting`. The most likely answer is that the Sheet was originally attached *before* the bug surfaced (so `setSetting` succeeded on a Postgres version/parser-state where the bareword was accepted), then a later version-bump or schema reload tightened parsing — and Catalog updates you saw were either pre-bug pushes or you were looking at a tab that hadn't actually refreshed in a while. Either way, both code paths now use the quoted identifier and will reliably resolve.

After restart, scan one item. You should see exactly one of these in the server log:

```
[Inventory] Received append → "<product>" qty=<n> (receipt=…)
```

If that line appears and the row still doesn't land in the Sheet, paste me whatever error follows. If you instead see one of the `skipped (…)` warnings, paste it and we'll fix the specific cause.

Found it. The bug is in my SQL comment — specifically the word **"didn't"**. The apostrophe in `didn't` (line 279) flips the placeholder normalizer's `inSingleQuote` state to true, and since it doesn't track `--` line comments, it stays in "inside a string" mode for the rest of the SQL. So the two `?` placeholders in `WHERE r.id = ? AND r.site_id = ?` are NEVER converted to `$1`/`$2`. Postgres sees the bare `?` and fails on the next token: `AND`.

  "file_path": "/Users/appointy/work/OfficeOperationsUmbrella/office-ops-engine/src/mastra/lib/database.ts",
  "old_string": "function replaceQuestionPlaceholders(sql: string): string {\n  let index = 0;\n  let output = \"\";\n  let inSingleQuote = false;\n  for (let i = 0; i < sql.length; i++) {\n    const char = sql[i];\n    const next = sql[i + 1];\n    if (char === \"'\" && next === \"'\") {\n      output += char + next;\n      i++;\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (char === \"'\") {\n      inSingleQuote = !inSingleQuote;\n      output += char;\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (char === \"?\" && !inSingleQuote) {\n      index++;\n      output += `$${index}`;\n      continue;\n    }\n    output += char;\n  }\n  return output;\n}",
  "new_string": "function replaceQuestionPlaceholders(sql: string): string {\n  let index = 0;\n  let output = \"\";\n  let inSingleQuote = false;\n  let inDoubleQuote = false;\n  let inLineComment = false;\n  let inBlockComment = false;\n  for (let i = 0; i < sql.length; i++) {\n    const char = sql[i];\n    const next = sql[i + 1];\n\n    // End of a -- line comment is the next newline; nothing else\n    // toggles state inside the comment.\n    if (inLineComment) {\n      output += char;\n      if (char === \"\\n\") inLineComment = false;\n      continue;\n    }\n    // End of /* … */ block comment.\n    if (inBlockComment) {\n      output += char;\n      if (char === \"*\" && next === \"/\") {\n        output += next;\n        i++;\n        inBlockComment = false;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n    // Doubled-quote escape inside a single-quoted string ('' = literal ').\n    if (inSingleQuote && char === \"'\" && next === \"'\") {\n      output += char + next;\n      i++;\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (char === \"'\" && !inDoubleQuote) {\n      inSingleQuote = !inSingleQuote;\n      output += char;\n      continue;\n    }\n    // Double-quoted identifiers (\"col name\") — we don't replace ? inside\n    // those either. Apostrophes inside don't toggle string state.\n    if (char === '\"' && !inSingleQuote) {\n      inDoubleQuote = !inDoubleQuote;\n      output += char;\n      continue;\n    }\n    // Start of a -- line comment.\n    if (!inSingleQuote && !inDoubleQuote && char === \"-\" && next === \"-\") {\n      inLineComment = true;\n      output += char;\n      continue;\n    }\n    // Start of a /* … */ block comment.\n    if (!inSingleQuote && !inDoubleQuote && char === \"/\" && next === \"*\") {\n      inBlockComment = true;\n      output += char;\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (char === \"?\" && !inSingleQuote && !inDoubleQuote) {\n      index++;\n      output += `$${index}`;\n      continue;\n    }\n    output += char;\n  }\n  return output;\n}"
}

> AGENT

Clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`** and scan one item.

**Root cause** — actually a two-part bug:

1. **My SQL comment had a literal apostrophe in "didn't".** Line comments (`-- …`) are fine in Postgres, but the driver's question-mark-to-`$N` normalizer doesn't know about comments. It tracked `'` as toggling string state, so the apostrophe in `didn't match` flipped `inSingleQuote` to true, and stayed true through the rest of the SQL. The `?` placeholders in `WHERE r.id = ? AND r.site_id = ?` were thought to be inside a string and never replaced. Postgres got literal `?` characters and choked on the next token: `AND`.

2. **The normalizer itself was naive.** Fixed it in `lib/database.ts` to be a proper SQL lexer: it now skips `--` line comments and `/* … */` block comments, also treats `"` double-quoted identifiers as opaque, and handles `''` escape sequences inside string literals. Future SQL comments with apostrophes, double-quoted identifiers, or block comments won't trip the same trap.

3. Both spots in `db.ts` (the per-receipt + the list compliance log) were patched — apostrophe-free comments, with a note pointing future readers at the normalizer.

After restart, scan an item. You should now see:

```
[Inventory] Received append → "<product name>" qty=<n> (receipt=…)
```

…and the row should appear in the Sheet's **Received** tab.

> DEVELOPER

are we storing all the other bill names of a product apart from standard name, so that when the same vendor
  bill is scanned next time we could check it and map or recommend to map to standard name?

> AGENT

Yes — that's exactly what `product_aliases` is.

**Schema:**
```
product_aliases:
  raw_name     TEXT  (the vendor's spelling, lowercased)
  product_id   FK → canonical_products.product_id
  hsn_code     optional context
  vendor_name  optional
  confidence   0–1
  source       admin_validated | hsn_fuzzy | llm_normalized | …
  + UNIQUE (site_id, raw_name, COALESCE(hsn_code,''))
```

**When rows are written:** every time you click **Validate & save** on the bill review screen, `processValidatedBill` saves an alias for each line where the bill text differs from the standard name:

```
if (item.bill_item_name.trim() !== canonicalName) {
  saveProductAlias({
    rawName: item.bill_item_name,
    productId: <standard product id>,
    hsnCode: item.hsn_code,
    confidence: 1.0,
    source: "admin_validated",
  });
}
```

Aliases also accumulate from the catalog suggester's HSN-fuzzy and LLM-normalized paths when those auto-match a bill line, and from the unresolved-resolve action on the dashboard.

**When they're read** (the matching pipeline, in order):
1. exact name match on `canonical_products.canonical_name`
2. **`findProductAlias(siteId, raw_name, hsn_code)`** — case-insensitive lookup on `product_aliases` — this is the cache hit you're asking about
3. HSN-scoped fuzzy match
4. LLM normalize
5. unresolved

So on every later bill upload, before any fuzzy/LLM work runs, the suggester checks the alias table for an exact `raw_name` (+ optional HSN). When it hits, that's an `exact` / `alias`-method suggestion with high confidence — which now (after the fix two turns ago) auto-applies on the bill review row and shows "✓ Matched to standard".

**Behaviour you'll see in practice:**
- First time a vendor writes `"Wagh Bakri 1kg bks1"` → suggester returns nothing certain → admin maps it to `"Wagh Bakri Chai 1kg"` and validates → alias row saved.
- Second time the same vendor sends the same name → suggester hits the alias → row arrives pre-mapped to `"Wagh Bakri Chai 1kg"`, green pill, no admin work needed.
- A different vendor writes the same product as `"W Bakri 1K"` → alias miss the first time; admin maps; that becomes a second alias on the same product. Over time each canonical product accumulates one alias per vendor spelling.

Two small things worth knowing about how strict the lookup is:
- Match is case-insensitive but otherwise byte-exact. `"Wagh Bakri 1kg bks1"` and `"Wagh Bakri 1kg bks2"` are two different aliases (different SR numbers in the bill).
- HSN-aware: the same `raw_name` can map to *different* products under different HSN contexts (e.g. `"Chai"` + HSN 0902 → tea, `"Chai"` + HSN 2106 → some other prepared beverage).

If you want a UI to **see/edit** the aliases attached to a standard product (audit what's been folded in, remove a wrong one without nuking everything via the existing "Clear learned aliases" button), I can add an expander in the Catalog tab — say the word.

\"—\"}</td>\n        <td style={td}>{p.unit}</td>\n        <td style={td}>{p.pack_size}</td>\n        <td style={td}>{p.created_at ? new Date(p.created_at).toLocaleDateString() : \"—\"}</td>\n      </tr>\n      {open && (\n        <tr style={{ background: \"var(--surface, #fafafa)\" }}>\n          <td></td>\n          <td colSpan={6} style={{ padding: \"8px 12px 12px\" }}>\n            <div style={{ fontSize: 11, color: \"var(--muted)\", marginBottom: 6, textTransform: \"uppercase\", letterSpacing: 0.5 }}>\n              Vendor names mapped to this standard product\n            </div>\n            {aliasesQuery.isLoading && (\n              <div style={{ fontSize: 12, color: \"var(--muted)\" }}>Loading…</div>\n            )}\n            {!aliasesQuery.isLoading && aliases.length === 0 && (\n              <div style={{ fontSize: 12, color: \"var(--muted)\", fontStyle: \"italic\" }}>\n                No vendor aliases yet. They accumulate as you validate bills with this product mapped.\n              </div>\n            )}\n            {aliases.length > 0 && (\n              <div style={{ display: \"grid\", gap: 4 }}>\n                {aliases.map((a) => (\n                  <div\n                    key={a.id}\n                    style={{\n                      display: \"grid\",\n                      gridTemplateColumns: \"1fr auto auto auto\",\n                      gap: 10,\n                      alignItems: \"center\",\n                      padding: \"4px 8px\",\n                      border: \"1px solid var(--line)\",\n                      borderRadius: 4,\n                      background: \"var(--surface, #fff)\",\n                      fontSize: 12,\n                    }}\n                  >\n                    <span style={{ fontFamily: \"ui-monospace, monospace\" }}>{a.raw_name}</span>\n                    <span style={{ color: \"var(--muted)\", fontSize: 11 }}>\n                      {a.hsn_code ? `HSN ${a.hsn_code}` : \"no HSN\"}\n                    </span>\n                    <span style={{ color: \"var(--muted)\", fontSize: 11 }}>\n                      {a.source} · {Math.round((Number(a.confidence) || 0) * 100)}%\n                    </span>\n                    <button\n                      type=\"button\"\n                      onClick={() => {\n                        if (confirm(`Remove this alias?\\n\\n\"${a.raw_name}\" → ${p.canonical_name}\\n\\nNext time a bill uses this name, the system won't auto-map it and the admin will have to pick again.`)) {\n                          deleteAliasMutation.mutate(a.id);\n                        }\n                      }}\n                      disabled={deleteAliasMutation.isPending}\n                      style={{ ...iconBtn, color: \"#dc2626\" }}\n                      title=\"Remove this alias\"\n                    >\n                      <Trash2 size={11} />\n                    </button>\n                  </div>\n                ))}\n              </div>\n            )}\n          </td>\n        </tr>\n      )}\n    </>\n  );\n}\n\n// ───────────────────────── Compliance ─────────────────────────"

> AGENT

Clean. **Restart `office-ops-engine`**, hard-reload the dashboard.

**What's added:**

- Catalog tab table now has a small chevron in the first column of every row. Click it to expand an inline panel beneath the row.
- The expander **lazy-loads** the aliases for that one product only when opened (`useQuery` with `enabled: open`), so the Catalog tab doesn't make N extra requests on render.
- Each alias renders as a one-line row showing the **vendor's raw name** (monospaced so you can see exact spelling/whitespace), the **HSN context** (or "no HSN"), and the **source + confidence** (`admin_validated · 100%`, `hsn_fuzzy · 78%`, etc.). A red trash icon on the right removes that single alias, with a confirm dialog explaining the consequence — next bill using that vendor name won't auto-resolve.
- Empty state: "No vendor aliases yet. They accumulate as you validate bills with this product mapped." So admins know it's normal for a fresh product.

**Backend changes:**
- `GET    /api/inventory/canonical-products/:id/aliases` — list aliases for that product (guard or admin auth ok).
- `DELETE /api/inventory/aliases/:id` — remove a single alias (admin only).
- `deleteProductAlias(aliasId)` helper in `db.ts`.

The existing "Clear learned aliases" nuke button stays on the Catalog tab header for the case where the whole alias cache is poisoned. Use the per-product expander when you only want to drop one bad mapping.

Clean. Hard-reload the dashboard.

**What changed:**

1. **Linked Google Sheet card — reformatted.** No more dense paragraph. The card now has:
   - A clean `<dl>` key/value grid: **Owner** / **Sheet ID** (monospace, muted, wraps cleanly) / **Tabs** (each tab as a small pill chip).
   - A small bulleted explanation underneath:
     > • **Ordered** — validated bills append here.  
     > • **Received** — every scanned receipt appends here.  
     > • **Catalog** — live snapshot of every standard product; refreshes on validate, create, and field registrations.
   - Action buttons (Open / Detach) stay on the right.

2. **Removed the "open" pill on Order cards.** `open` is the default state of every newly-created order and the card layout already implies "expected, awaiting delivery". Now:
   - `open` → no pill (cleanest, less noise)
   - `partial` → amber "partial" pill
   - `done` → green "done" pill
   - any other status (future-proofing) → neutral pill

3. **Inline Status legend on the Export tab**, just above the table:
   > **Status legend:** [OK] guard scanned without raising a flag · [Flagged] guard marked a mismatch (wrong qty, damaged pack, bad expiry…)
   
   So admins know what OK / Flagged mean at a glance without hovering the column header. The header `title` tooltip stays for redundancy.

> AGENT

Clean. Restart `office-ops-engine`.

**Audit result:**

I cross-referenced every `CREATE TABLE` in `postgres-schema.ts` (53 tables in total) against the four lists in `lib/database.ts`. Every table is in exactly one bucket — no schema table is unreachable by any reset command.

**Coverage map:**

- `INVENTORY_RESET_TABLES` (15) — `inventory_receipts · inventory_mismatch_flags · unresolved_bill_items · inventory_order_items · inventory_orders · inventory_reorder_requests · inventory_issues · inventory_stock · inventory_products · inventory · inventory_name_aliases · product_barcodes · product_aliases · canonical_products · inventory_settings`
- `VISITOR_RESET_TABLES` (13) — `visitor_sos_events · visitor_invitation_stakeholders · visitor_audit_log · expected_guest_snapshots · visitor_sessions · offline_sync_events · guard_sessions · guard_push_subscriptions · visitor_broadcasts · visitor_invitations · visitor_locations · visitors · guards`
- `ALL_DATA_TABLES_EXCEPT_FLOWS_AND_AUTH` (28) = inventory + visitor + `asset_history · assets · facility_requests · cafeteria_order_items · cafeteria_orders · cafeteria_menu_items · sop_tasks · staff_attendance · staff_channels · staff · raw_messages · sheets_sync_events · audit_log · in_app_notifications`
- `FLOW_AND_AUTH_TABLES` (12) — `flow_executions · flow_rules · flow_graphs · password_reset_otps · slack_config · visitor_rules · visitor_templates · role_permissions · user_roles · permissions · roles · users`

**Telegram confirmation messages updated** to spell out exactly what each command wipes and what it preserves, including the newer-added inventory tables (`canonical_products`, `product_aliases`, `product_barcodes`, `unresolved_bill_items`, `inventory_settings`) that earlier copy mentioned only generically:

- `/reset_inventory` now explicitly calls out the standard catalog + barcodes + aliases + linked-Sheet ID/owner.
- `/reset_visitor` now explicitly notes that visitor_rules + visitor_templates are *flow config* and not touched.
- `/reset_all` lists the full operational scope (admin reads it once and knows the blast radius).
- `/wipeout` explicitly names which preserved-on-reset-all tables it now also nukes (flows, users, roles, OTPs, visitor rules/templates).

If you add a new table to `postgres-schema.ts` later, the rule of thumb: add it to one of the four lists in `lib/database.ts` — don't leave it dangling. The pattern is also resilient if you forget — `deleteTables(...)` swallows `relation does not exist` per-table so adding it to a list before the migration runs won't break the command, it'll just show up as `skipped` in the result message.

Admin can still type a\n// custom one — these are just suggestions to keep naming consistent\n// across products and across vendors.\nconst CATEGORY_SEED = [\n  \"Beverages\",\n  \"Snacks\",\n  \"Bakery\",\n  \"Dairy\",\n  \"Frozen\",\n  \"Pantry / Grocery\",\n  \"Fruits & Vegetables\",\n  \"Cleaning\",\n  \"Personal Care\",\n  \"Cafeteria\",\n  \"Office\",\n  \"Stationery\",\n  \"Other\",\n];\n\n/**\n * Text-backed numeric input — fixes three classes of pain with the\n * built-in <input type=\"number\">:\n *   1. Admin couldn't fully clear the field (auto-coerce-to-0/1 fought\n *      the empty state). Now you can type, backspace to blank, paste\n *      freely; we only normalise on blur.\n *   2. Scroll-wheel-changes-the-value. People scrolling the page would\n *      silently change qty/rate. We use type=\"text\" so the wheel\n *      doesn't touch it; inputMode=\"decimal\" still gets the right\n *      mobile keyboard.\n *   3. Spinner arrows (the up/down stepper) — gone for the same reason.\n *\n * On blur, an empty value falls back to 0 per spec.\n */\nfunction NumericInput({\n  value,\n  onChange,\n  onBlur,\n  fallback = 0,\n  style,\n  ...rest\n}: {\n  value: number;\n  onChange: (v: number) => void;\n  onBlur?: () => void;\n  fallback?: number;\n  style?: React.CSSProperties;\n} & Omit<React.InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>, \"value\" | \"onChange\" | \"onBlur\" | \"style\" | \"type\">) {\n  const [text, setText] = useState<string>(String(value ?? fallback));\n\n  // Re-sync the local buffer when the parent's value changes from\n  // outside (e.g. a catalog suggestion auto-fills the row).\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const expected = String(value ?? fallback);\n    setText((cur) => (Number(cur) === Number(expected) ? cur : expected));\n  }, [value, fallback]);\n\n  return (\n    <input\n      type=\"text\"\n      inputMode=\"decimal\"\n      autoComplete=\"off\"\n      value={text}\n      onChange={(e) => {\n        const raw = e.target.value;\n        if (raw === \"\" || /^-?\\d*\\.?\\d*$/.test(raw)) {\n          setText(raw);\n          // Intermediate states like \"\" / \"-\" / \".\" aren't pushed up.\n          if (raw !== \"\" && raw !== \"-\" && raw !== \".\") {\n            const n = Number(raw);\n            if (Number.isFinite(n)) onChange(n);\n          }\n        }\n      }}\n      onBlur={() => {\n        if (text === \"\" || text === \"-\" || text === \".\") {\n          setText(String(fallback));\n          onChange(fallback);\n        }\n        onBlur?.();\n      }}\n      style={style}\n      {...rest}\n    />\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Category combobox — typed input with a dropdown of category\n * suggestions. Seeds from CATEGORY_SEED plus every distinct category\n * already used in the catalog, so admin-added customs become part of\n * the suggestion pool naturally.\n */\nfunction CategoryCombobox({\n  value,\n  catalog,\n  onChange,\n  style,\n}: {\n  value: string;\n  catalog: CanonicalProduct[];\n  onChange: (v: string) => void;\n  style?: React.CSSProperties;\n}) {\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n  const [activeIdx, setActiveIdx] = useState(0);\n  const wrapRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    function onDocClick(e: MouseEvent) {\n      if (!wrapRef.current) return;\n      if (!wrapRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) setOpen(false);\n    }\n    document.addEventListener(\"mousedown\", onDocClick);\n    return () => document.removeEventListener(\"mousedown\", onDocClick);\n  }, []);\n\n  const options = useMemo(() => {\n    const used = new Set<string>();\n    for (const p of catalog) {\n      const c = (p.category ?? \"\").trim();\n      if (c) used.add(c);\n    }\n    // Union: seed list + any custom categories already in the catalog.\n    const merged = [...new Set([...CATEGORY_SEED, ...Array.from(used)])];\n    const q = value.trim().toLowerCase();\n    if (!q) return merged.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));\n    return merged\n      .filter((c) => c.toLowerCase().includes(q))\n      .sort((a, b) => {\n        const al = a.toLowerCase();\n        const bl = b.toLowerCase();\n        const aStarts = al.startsWith(q) ? 0 : 1;\n        const bStarts = bl.startsWith(q) ? 0 : 1;\n        if (aStarts !== bStarts) return aStarts - bStarts;\n        return a.localeCompare(b);\n      });\n  }, [catalog, value]);\n\n  function commit(c: string) {\n    onChange(c);\n    setOpen(false);\n    setActiveIdx(0);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div ref={wrapRef} style={{ position: \"relative\" }}>\n      <input\n        type=\"text\"\n        value={value}\n        onChange={(e) => { onChange(e.target.value); setOpen(true); setActiveIdx(0); }}\n        onFocus={() => setOpen(true)}\n        onKeyDown={(e) => {\n          if (e.key === \"ArrowDown\") { e.preventDefault(); setOpen(true); setActiveIdx((i) => Math.min(options.length - 1, i + 1)); }\n          else if (e.key === \"ArrowUp\") { e.preventDefault(); setActiveIdx((i) => Math.max(0, i - 1)); }\n          else if (e.key === \"Enter\" && open && options[activeIdx]) { e.preventDefault(); commit(options[activeIdx]); }\n          else if (e.key === \"Escape\") { setOpen(false); }\n        }}\n        placeholder=\"Type or pick a category…\"\n        autoComplete=\"off\"\n        style={style ?? input}\n      />\n      {open && options.length > 0 && (\n        <div\n          style={{\n            position: \"absolute\",\n            top: \"calc(100% + 2px)\",\n            left: 0,\n            right: 0,\n            zIndex: 30,\n            maxHeight: 200,\n            overflowY: \"auto\",\n            background: \"var(--surface, #fff)\",\n            border: \"1px solid var(--line)\",\n            borderRadius: 6,\n            boxShadow: \"0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)\",\n          }}\n        >\n          {options.map((c, i) => (\n            <div\n              key={c}\n              onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); commit(c); }}\n              onMouseEnter={() => setActiveIdx(i)}\n              style={{\n                padding: \"5px 10px\",\n                cursor: \"pointer\",\n                background: i === activeIdx ? \"var(--line)\" : \"transparent\",\n                fontSize: 12,\n              }}\n            >\n              {c}\n            </div>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  );\n}"
